SEC 02

High Concept

⟨ SYSTEM NOTIFICATION ⟩

You are the weakest hunter alive — an E-rank nobody who shouldn't survive. After a catastrophic dungeon incident, a mysterious System awakens inside you. Now you can level up when no one else can, extract shadows from the dead, and climb from the bottom of humanity to the throne of the Shadow Monarch.

One-Line Pitch

"The weakest hunter awakens a System no one else has — and the shadows of every enemy he kills will rise to fight for him."

Elevator Pitch

In a world where portals called Gates connect Earth to monster-filled dungeons, hunters are ranked from E to S. You are the weakest — barely surviving D-rank gates. But after a near-death encounter, a mysterious System binds to you. It gives you quests, stats, and the power to extract shadows from defeated enemies. As you grow, so does your shadow army — and so does the attention of those who fear what you're becoming.

Core Fantasy

  • Go from zero to god — feel the gap between E-rank and Monarch
  • Command an army of shadows — every kill becomes a soldier
  • Be the only one — no one else has the System
  • Earn everything — no shortcuts, no handouts, pure grind
SEC 03

Game Pillars

Every design decision must serve at least one of these five pillars.

⚔️

Solo Ascension

You start weak. Every stat point, skill, and shadow is earned alone. No party, no carry — pure personal growth.

👥

Shadow Army

Your power grows by commanding the dead. Build, upgrade, and deploy your own shadow army.

📋

The System

A living UI that guides, rewards, and punishes. It is the voice of the game — cold, absolute, and always watching.

📈

Feel the Gap

E-rank → S-rank progression must feel earned and massive. The player should feel unstoppable by the end.

🌑

Dark Fantasy World

Gates, monsters, corrupted hunters — danger everywhere. The world is hostile and unforgiving.

SEC 04

Core Gameplay Loop

Macro Loop

ENTER GATE → CLEAR DUNGEON → EXTRACT SHADOWS → LEVEL UP
    ↑                                                         ↓
←────── SPEND STATS / SKILLS / SHADOW UPGRADES ←

Moment-to-Moment

  1. Explore — Move through dungeon rooms, discover loot, avoid traps
  2. Fight — Real-time action combat against monsters
  3. Extract — Defeat boss → attempt shadow extraction
  4. Reward — System grants XP, gold, essence, skill points
  5. Upgrade — Allocate stats, unlock skills, upgrade shadows
  6. Repeat — Enter harder gate, push further

Session-to-Session Loop

  • Daily Quests — System gives daily tasks. Fail → Penalty Zone
  • Gate Rotation — New gates appear every in-game day
  • Rank Progression — Rank-up trials unlock new content
  • Shadow Growth — Army expands, new shadows to level
  • Story Beats — Main quest advances the narrative

Long-Term Loop

  • Act 1 — Awakening (E → D rank)
  • Act 2 — Rise (D → B rank)
  • Act 3 — Monarch (B → S rank)
  • Endgame — National level, Monarch trials, NG+

5.2 Hunter Ranks

E D C B A S MONARCH
⟨ SELECT A RANK ⟩

Click any rank above to view its progression details.

5.3 Rank-Up Trials

Each rank-up requires a trial — a special dungeon that tests a specific skill:

  • E→D: Survive a wave of monsters solo
  • D→C: Defeat a boss without using potions
  • C→B: Clear a dungeon using only shadows
  • B→A: Defeat a hunter-turned-monster (story)
  • A→S: Defeat a Monarch's vessel
  • S→MONARCH: Final trial — the System itself

5.4 Classes / Job Change

At level 20 (D-rank), the System offers a Job Change Quest. Player chooses one class:

🌑 CANON

Shadow Monarch

Shadow army focus. Highest shadow cap, strongest extraction, unique shadow skills.

🗡️

Assassin

Speed, crit, stealth. Lower shadow cap but higher personal DPS. Dodge-based.

🛡️

Berserker

Raw damage, tanky, lifesteal. Frontline bruiser. Limited shadow support.

🔮

Mage

AoE spells, elemental damage, crowd control. Moderate shadow cap. Glass cannon.

Note: All classes can extract shadows, but only Shadow Monarch gets full army potential. Other classes are for NG+ or alt playthroughs.

6.6 Boss Design Philosophy

  • Telegraphed attacks — clear wind-up animations

  • Story weight — bosses are characters, not just walls
SEC 07

Shadow Army System

⟨ SYSTEM ALERT — SIGNATURE MECHANIC ⟩

The signature mechanic. Every enemy you defeat can be extracted as a shadow soldier. Shadows fight for you, level up, and evolve. Bosses become named shadows with unique abilities.

Interactive · Try Shadow Extraction

💀
AWAITING COMMAND
→ Click the target to attempt extraction

7.1 Extraction

  • Triggered after defeating an enemy (not all enemies are extractable)
  • Base chance: 30% for grunts, 50% for elites, 100% for bosses
  • Modified by: Shadow Affinity skill, Intelligence stat, enemy rank
  • Visual: Enemy dissolves into black mist → shadow rises with glowing eyes
  • Failed extraction: Enemy is gone, no shadow gained

7.2 Shadow Ranks

RankSourceCapSpecial
CommonGruntsUnlimitedBasic attacks only
EliteElite enemiesUnlimited1 skill
CommanderMini-bosses52 skills, aura buff
MarshalBosses (named)33 skills, unique ultimate
MonarchStory bosses1Fully unique, story-bound

7.3 Shadow Roles

🛡️ Tank

High HP, taunt, shield. Draws aggro. Examples: Golem, Knight.

⚔️ DPS

High damage, low HP. Melee or ranged. Examples: Assassin, Archer.

🔮 Mage

AoE, elemental, crowd control. Examples: Dark Mage, Shaman.

💚 Support

Heals, buffs, cleanses. Examples: Priest, Healer.

🐺 Beast

Fast, aggressive, pack tactics. Examples: Wolf, Drake.

7.4 Named Shadows (Examples)

NameRoleOriginSignature Ability
KaelTankFirst boss (Gate Guardian)Iron Bulwark — taunts all enemies, gains shield
VexDPSElite AssassinShadow Strike — teleports to weakest enemy, executes
MorrowMageCaster BossVoid Nova — AoE explosion, slows enemies
GrimBeastMonster BossFrenzy — attack speed +100% for 5s
SeraphineSupportCorrupted HealerDark Mend — heals all shadows, cleanses debuffs

7.5 Shadow Upgrades

  • Level Up — Spend Shadow Essence to level a shadow (max = player level)
  • Rank Up — Common → Elite → Commander (rare materials)
  • Skill Unlock — Higher ranks unlock more skills
  • Evolution — Some shadows have alternate forms (e.g., Grim → Grim Alpha)

7.6 Shadow Command System

CommandEffectCooldown
AttackShadows focus targetNone
DefendShadows guard player, +defenseNone
FocusAll shadows target one enemy5s
RecallShadows return to Shadow RealmNone
UltimateAll shadows use their ultimate60s

7.7 Shadow Realm (Storage)

  • A pocket dimension where unused shadows wait
  • Accessible from the hub city
  • Shadows here can be upgraded, sorted, released
  • Visual: dark void with floating shadow figures
  • Capacity: 50 base, expandable to 200
SEC 08

The System — UI Layer

⟨ SYSTEM CORE ⟩

The System is not just a menu — it is a character. It speaks, it judges, it rewards, and it punishes. Every interaction should feel like the System is watching.

8.1 Visual Design

ElementStyle
ColorCyan-blue holographic (#00d4ff → #9c4dff gradient)
FontMonospace / retro-futuristic
AnimationFade in + slide + glow pulse
SoundDigital chime, soft beep, low hum
BorderThin glowing line, corner brackets

8.2 System Windows

Status Window

  • Name, Level, Rank, Class
  • HP, MP, Stamina bars
  • Stat list (STR, AGI, VIT, INT, PER)
  • Skill list
  • Shadow army summary
  • Accessible via Tab or menu

Quest Window

  • Active quests (Main, Side, Daily)
  • Objective tracker
  • Reward preview
  • Timer for dailies

Notification Pop-ups

  • "You have leveled up."
  • "New skill available."
  • "Shadow extraction successful."
  • "Daily quest incomplete. Penalty will begin in 1 hour."
  • "You have entered a Red Gate."

Store Window

  • Buy items with Gold
  • Buy skills with Skill Points
  • Buy shadow upgrades with Shadow Essence
  • Limited stock (refreshes daily)

8.3 Daily Quest System

QuestRequirementRewardPenalty
Physical TrainingComplete 1 dungeon500 XP, 200 GoldPenalty Zone
Shadow MaintenanceUpgrade 1 shadow100 EssenceLost essence
Hunter's DutyKill 50 enemies1 Skill PointPenalty Zone
SurvivalClear 1 gate without dying300 XP, 150 GoldPenalty Zone

Penalty Zone

  • Forced survival dungeon — no rewards, only survival
  • Monsters are 2x player level
  • Death = lose 10% XP
  • Cannot leave until cleared or timer expires
  • Purpose: Adds tension, encourages daily play

8.4 System Voice / Personality

  • Tone: Cold, absolute, neutral
  • Never says "please" or "sorry"
  • Speaks in short sentences
  • Examples:
    • "You have been chosen."
    • "Complete the quest. Failure is not an option."
    • "Your shadow army grows."
    • "The System acknowledges your strength."

SEC 14

MVP Scope & Roadmap

⟨ SYSTEM DIRECTIVE ⟩

Rule: Ship small, ship often. Each phase must be playable. No feature creep.

Phase 1 — Prototype 4–8 weeks

  • 1 playable dungeon (cave theme)
  • Basic combat (attack, dodge, 1 skill)
  • 1 enemy type (grunt)
  • 1 boss (Stone Golem)
  • 1 shadow extraction
  • Basic System UI (status window)

Phase 2 — Vertical Slice 2–3 months

  • 3 dungeons (cave, ruins, ice)
  • 5 shadows (1 named: Kael)
  • Stat / level system
  • Skill tree (10 skills)
  • Shadow army management
  • System UI (quests, notifications)
  • Save / load
  • Hub city (basic)

Phase 3 — Alpha 3–6 months

  • 10+ dungeons
  • Rank progression E→C
  • Story Act 1
  • Daily quest system
  • Penalty Zone
  • Named shadows (3)
  • Boss variety (5 bosses)
  • Audio pass

Phase 4 — Beta / Early Access 6–12 months

  • Full Act 1–2
  • Rank progression E→A
  • Red Gates, Double Dungeons
  • Named shadows (8+)
  • Full skill tree (30+ skills)
  • Polish, balance, optimization
  • Steam page + wishlist push

Phase 5 — 1.0 Launch 12–18 months

  • Full story (Act 1–3)
  • All ranks E→MONARCH
  • NG+ mode
  • All shadow ranks + named shadows
  • Full audio + localization
  • Post-launch support plan

Each environment also has its own blockout-to-polish roadmap in Level Plans & Visual References. Campaign placement and inclusion in these release phases remain open.

Moonfall Sanctuary — Valley of the Silver Cascades

An ancient waterfall sanctuary awakened beneath an enormous rose-colored moon

Primary objective: Follow the Moonwater River through the valley, awaken the three Lunar Shrines, reach the upper sacred grove, defeat or pacify its guardian, and activate the Moonblossom Sanctuary

Read full production specification · 19 sections
A. LEVEL OVERVIEW
CategoryProduction Definition
Level NameMoonfall Sanctuary — Valley of the Silver Cascades
Level CategoryMystical mountain valley / traversal / exploration / sacred encounter
ThemeAn ancient waterfall sanctuary awakened beneath an enormous rose-colored moon
Gameplay TypeExploration → river traversal → vertical ascent → shrine discovery → guardian encounter → sacred-tree transition
Primary ObjectiveFollow the Moonwater River through the valley, awaken the three Lunar Shrines, reach the upper sacred grove, defeat or pacify its guardian, and activate the Moonblossom Sanctuary
Main LandmarkMulti-tier waterfall wall beneath the giant pink moon
Secondary LandmarksHero cherry trees, turquoise river basin, black cliff pillars, stone bridge, ruined shrine, upper waterfall ledges

Reference elements that must remain unchanged

The final level should preserve the huge moon above the cliffs, multiple long waterfalls, dark steep rock walls, broad reflective river, foreground boulders, pink blossom trees framing both sides, mist around waterfall bases and the strong blue/pink nighttime palette.

B. SPATIAL & GAMEPLAY SPECIFICATION
Overall layout

The environment is structured as a valley journey moving from low elevation to high elevation:

Z01 Valley Entrance → Z02 Moonwater River → Z03 Central Cascade Basin → Z04 Ancient Shrine → Z05 Upper Falls → Z06 Moonblossom Grove → Z07 Sanctuary Transition

The waterfalls and moon provide continuous orientation. The player should rarely feel lost even when optional branches are available.

Z01 — Valley Entrance

Purpose: Establish the environment and immediately reveal the moon and waterfall wall.

Gameplay function: Safe orientation area and movement introduction.

Visual landmark: Framing cherry trees and the distant waterfalls.

Traversal: Ground movement, shallow water, small rocks.

Combat: None.

Environmental storytelling: Broken pilgrimage markers indicate the valley was once visited regularly.

Z02 — Moonwater River

Purpose: Bring the player gradually deeper into the valley.

Gameplay function: Exploration and first optional route.

Traversal: Riverbank paths, stepping stones, shallow crossings and small natural bridges.

Primary visual feature: Moonlight reflecting through turquoise water.

Encounter: Small ambient enemies or corrupted wildlife where appropriate.

Secondary Route

A raised path follows the left cliff and reaches an abandoned shrine overlooking the river.

Optional Route

A small waterfall cave behind a side cascade contains a collectible or lore object.

Z03 — Central Cascade Basin

This is the largest lower-level open area.

Purpose: Navigation hub.

Gameplay function: Exploration, first significant combat, route selection.

Visual feature: Multiple waterfalls dropping into one broad pool.

Encounter type: Moderate enemy encounter or guardian patrol.

Traversal: Shallow water, boulders, rock shelves and wooden crossing structures.

From this location the player can clearly identify:

  • Upper Falls
  • Ancient Shrine
  • Moonblossom Grove
  • Main ascent route
Z04 — Ancient Moon Shrine

Purpose: Environmental storytelling and progression objective.

Gameplay function: Activate Lunar Shrine 01/02 depending on route order.

Visual feature: Small weathered stone pavilion built into the cliff.

Encounter: Shrine guardian or environmental puzzle.

Interaction: Rotate or align a lunar mechanism so moonlight reaches the altar.

Activating the shrine changes subtle environmental lighting and causes particles to travel upstream toward the sacred grove.

Z05 — Upper Falls

Purpose: Main vertical traversal section.

Gameplay function: Climbing, platforming and elevated combat.

Visual features: Narrow ledges beside major waterfalls, wooden platforms, bridge remnants and elevated cherry trees.

Traversal sequence:

Lower ledge → stone shelf → waterfall-side stair → broken bridge → upper plateau.

The player should repeatedly look back over the lower valley so the ascent feels significant.

Z06 — Moonblossom Grove

Purpose: Primary climax area.

Visual feature: Large sacred cherry tree positioned against the moon.

Gameplay function: Boss encounter, ritual or narrative confrontation.

Proposed encounter: Guardian of the Moonblossom.

The arena is primarily natural stone and shallow water rather than an artificially obvious circular boss platform.

Phase 1

Guardian fights across the open grove.

Phase 2

Cherry petals become supernatural particles and water channels illuminate.

Phase 3

Moonlight intensifies, waterfall mist expands around the perimeter and glowing roots create temporary hazard lanes.

Z07 — Sanctuary Transition

After the encounter, the sacred tree activates.

A moonlit passage, shrine gate or water-based portal opens behind it and transitions the player into the next environment.

PRIMARY, SECONDARY AND OPTIONAL ROUTES
Primary Route

Valley Entrance → River → Central Basin → Upper Falls → Moonblossom Grove.

Secondary Route

Central Basin → Ancient Shrine → cliff route → reconnect at Upper Falls.

Optional Route

Waterfall cave → collectible/lore → shortcut back to Central Basin.

Secret Area

A concealed shrine behind the largest waterfall containing a rare progression item.

CHECKPOINTS

CP01: Central Cascade Basin.

CP02: Ancient Moon Shrine.

CP03: Upper Falls immediately before Moonblossom Grove.

CP04: Post-guardian sanctuary.

PLAYABLE BOUNDARIES

Use natural geometry wherever possible:

  • steep cliff walls;
  • deep river channels;
  • heavy waterfall flow;
  • dense rock formations;
  • inaccessible canopy;
  • mountain ridges;
  • mist-covered drops.

Background cliffs must not visually suggest walkable paths unless gameplay supports them.

HAZARDS

Falling from elevated waterfall paths.

Deep-water areas.

Powerful waterfall currents.

Slippery or collapsing stone ledges where appropriate.

Temporary magical root hazards during the final encounter.

H. LIGHTING SPECIFICATION

The dominant visual contrast is cool blue moonlit terrain against warm pink blossoms and moonlight accents.

Primary Light

Moon-driven directional light.

Direction: upper-left toward lower-right.

Color: cool lavender-blue.

Fill Light

Soft blue Skylight from the night environment.

Rim Lighting

Strong silver-blue rim on wet rocks and waterfall edges.

Focal Lighting

Pink/lavender moon glow on the blossom canopy and sacred grove.

Exposure

Cinematic low-light exposure while preserving waterfall whites.

Avoid clipping the moon and waterfalls simultaneously.

Shadows

Deep but softly filled; cliff silhouettes should feel massive without becoming unreadable.

UE5 Systems

Directional Light, Sky Light, Sky Atmosphere, Volumetric Clouds, Exponential Height Fog, Volumetric Fog, Lumen GI/reflections and Post Process Volume.

J. ENVIRONMENTAL STORYTELLING

The valley should suggest that it was once a sacred pilgrimage destination devoted to lunar renewal.

Broken stone markers trace the old pilgrimage route.

Ancient steps disappear beneath the river.

Shrines face the moon rather than the waterfalls.

Cherry trees grow strongest around ritual locations.

Collapsed wooden platforms imply the valley was once actively maintained.

Offerings remain inside protected shrine recesses.

Water damage, moss and mineral streaks communicate centuries of abandonment.

The sacred tree appears unusually healthy compared with surrounding vegetation.

Environmental storytelling density should increase near shrines and decrease along major combat/traversal paths.

Audio Opportunities

Waterfall roar should dominate the basin.

Higher routes gradually reduce low waterfall frequencies and reveal wind.

Cherry groves add leaf movement and subtle chimes.

Shrines introduce low harmonic tones.

The final grove should briefly become unnaturally quiet before the encounter.

N. COLLISION / NAVIGATION / GAMEPLAY READABILITY

Use simplified collision for cliff surfaces except explicitly traversable ledges.

Keep riverbed collision smooth enough that characters do not snag on decorative stones.

Large waterfall areas should use invisible blockers where the current visually implies an impassable force.

Use Nav Modifier Volumes around deep water.

Keep cherry-tree roots away from core combat lanes unless they intentionally define the arena.

Water reflections must not hide enemy silhouettes.

Path edges should use rock shape, blossom placement and moonlight to subtly guide the player.

P. PERFORMANCE STRATEGY

The largest expected performance costs are water rendering, waterfall translucency, Niagara spray, volumetric mist, blossom foliage, Lumen reflections and large Nanite cliff coverage.

Use Nanite for cliffs, boulders and architectural stone rather than foliage requiring complex animation.

Use HISM for secondary cherry trees and distant conifers.

Hero cherry trees should be hand placed.

Keep Niagara mist volumes localized instead of filling the entire valley with translucent particles.

Use distance-based VFX scalability for waterfall spray.

Reduce water reflection quality outside the central playable river.

Use simple background waterfall materials at long distance.

Restrict shadow-casting lights; most lighting should come from the moon and Skylight.

Use HLOD/culling for distant cliffs and trees.

Reserve high-complexity wet-rock shaders for foreground and traversable surfaces.

The most important profiling location is the Central Basin looking toward all major waterfalls, because that camera combines water, Nanite cliffs, foliage, mist, reflections and moon lighting in one frame.

Q. DEVELOPMENT ROADMAP
Stage 1 — Blockout

Establish valley footprint, river, cliffs, major waterfalls, central basin, ascent and grove.

Stage 2 — Gameplay Validation

Test traversal width, water depth, jumping, climbing, combat spaces, camera sightlines and route clarity.

Stage 3 — Structural Environment

Replace blockout cliffs, riverbanks, shrine architecture, bridges and main waterfall formations.

Stage 4 — Asset & Material Production

Create rocks, trees, hero shrine, sacred tree, props, wet-rock shaders, blossom materials and water treatments.

Stage 5 — Lighting & Atmosphere

Implement moon sky, night lighting, mist, waterfall fog, reflections, blossom highlights and final grading.

Stage 6 — Gameplay Implementation

Implement shrines, water currents, checkpoints, optional paths, guardian logic, grove transformation and final transition.

Stage 7 — Optimization & Polish

Profile GPU/CPU, Nanite, Lumen, water, Niagara, foliage, volumetrics, collision and streaming; finish environmental storytelling and cinematic presentation.

FINAL VALIDATION CHECKLIST
  • Giant rose moon remains a dominant celestial landmark.
  • Waterfalls preserve their reference positions and silhouette hierarchy.
  • Pink blossom trees frame rather than obstruct the valley.
  • Dark cliffs retain strong blue-grey visual mass.
  • Turquoise water remains visually distinct from the cliffs.
  • Main objective is readable from major vistas.
  • Top-down layout matches the hero environment.
  • Elevation progression corresponds to the same physical valley.
  • Upper Falls visibly connect to the lower basin.
  • Shrine route reconnects to the primary ascent.
  • Sacred Grove logically occupies the upper level.
  • Player scale remains consistent.
  • All dimensions are treated as proposed blockout values.
  • Modular cliff/shrine pieces fit established grid rules.
  • Water collision is smooth.
  • Deep water and safe shallow water are visually distinct.
  • Enemy silhouettes remain readable against waterfall mist.
  • Boss VFX preserve combat telegraphs.
  • Niagara systems use distance culling.
  • Blossom foliage has scalability settings.
  • Lumen reflections meet performance budget.
  • Distant waterfalls use simplified rendering.
  • Background cliffs remain non-playable.
  • Level streaming into the next environment is verified.
  • Final lighting maintains the blue/cyan/pink reference palette.
  • Poster, level layout and production specification all describe the same environment.
Open Design Questions
  • PC target frame rate.
  • Third-person or first-person player camera.
  • Whether the player supports swimming.
  • Exact climbing/mantling capability.
  • Whether shrine objectives are mandatory or partly optional.
  • Whether the Moonblossom Guardian must be defeated or can be pacified.
  • Intended total level duration.
  • Desired combat density versus exploration density.
  • Multiplayer/co-op requirements.
  • Whether the sanctuary exit uses seamless streaming or a cinematic transition.

Observed: the reference shows a lone player approaching a large circular platform through a broken elevated stone causeway, with a monumental citadel directly beyond it.

Inferred: the circular platform naturally reads as the primary combat/ritual arena.

Proposed: the arena becomes the level’s boss encounter and activation space.

B. Spatial & Gameplay Specification
Overall Layout

The level is organized around one dominant axial composition:

Player Spawn → Ruined Causeway → Outer Ring → Ascension Arena → Portal Dais → Citadel Gate

The main path should remain almost perfectly aligned with the portal and citadel so the player continuously understands the destination.

Z01 — Shattered Approach

Purpose: establish scale and reveal the citadel.

Gameplay: safe traversal with minimal combat.

Visual feature: broken wet stone path suspended above clouds, hanging chains, cyan braziers, red banners.

Traversal: walking, short jumps over fractured sections, optional ledges.

Encounter: none or very light ranged pressure.

Z02 — Broken Sentinel Causeway

Purpose: increase tension before the arena.

Gameplay: first hostile encounter and traversal hazard.

Visual feature: collapsed masonry and suspended fragments.

Traversal: narrow bridge segments, fractured floor edges.

Encounter: 3–6 enemies or one elite guardian.

Z03 — Outer Sanctuary Ring

Purpose: decompression and limited exploration before the central fight.

Gameplay: optional lore, consumables, upgrade/reward pickup, checkpoint.

Visual feature: perimeter statues, braziers, rune channels, red-leaf trees.

Traversal: circular movement around arena.

Encounter: optional enemies or inactive statues.

Z04 — Ascension Arena

Purpose: principal combat space.

Gameplay: boss / multi-phase encounter.

Visual feature: cyan concentric magical runes around a crimson axial energy line.

Traversal: broad circular movement with readable combat lanes.

Encounter: Astral Gate Warden.

Z05 — Portal Dais

Purpose: encounter climax and objective interaction.

Gameplay: activate/stabilize portal after boss defeat.

Visual feature: vertical crimson beam framed by gothic portal architecture.

Interaction: ritual activation, cinematic transition.

Z06 — Citadel Threshold

Purpose: end-of-level transition.

Gameplay: short walk into the next streamed level or cinematic.

Visual feature: monumental gate, statues, crimson energy curtain.

Routes

Primary Route: direct causeway into arena, always visible from spawn.

Secondary Route: partial perimeter path around the left or right side of the arena providing lore, consumables, or an advantageous pre-fight position.

Optional Route: fractured side platform connected to a smaller floating ruin containing a reward.

Secret Area: hidden beneath a damaged outer-ring stair or behind a broken statue plinth.

Exit: citadel portal after objective completion.

Playable Boundaries

Walkable geometry should remain on the main causeway, arena, perimeter ring, portal dais, and one optional side platform.

Most distant floating islands are background-only. They should not visually suggest reachable traversal unless a later level uses them.

Cloud volume and void beneath the level act as the natural world boundary.

Hazards

Falling from the platform.

Temporary astral fissures during boss phases.

Crimson beam sweep or portal discharge.

Violet corruption eruptions along damaged arena edges.

Collapsing floor sectors in the final boss phase.

E. Hero Asset Specifications
HA-01 — Ascension Portal

Purpose: final objective and visual focal point.

Placement: directly on the level’s central axis behind the arena.

Scale: proposed 16 m wide × 32 m high.

Mesh type: Nanite-compatible gothic arch plus separate animated energy components.

Collision: simplified architectural collision only.

Interaction: locked before boss defeat; activation after arena controller state changes.

Animation: rotating inner rune rings, energy buildup, beam stabilization.

Destruction: no full destruction; optional crack propagation.

Materials: black stone, oxidized metal details, emissive crimson energy.

VFX: vertical beam, energy motes, volumetric glow, sparks, lens bloom.

Reuse: unique.

HA-02 — Citadel Facade

Use a modular gothic architectural kit for towers, buttresses, arches, spires and walls, then assemble into one unique hero silhouette.

The player does not need access to most facade geometry in this level.

HA-03 — Rune Arena

Create as a modular stone floor plus decal/material-driven magical rings rather than baking every rune into unique geometry.

Boss phase logic should independently control concentric rune bands.

HA-04 — Guardian Statues

Four large hooded sentinels around the arena perimeter.

Use one master sculpt with 2–3 pose/head/weapon variations.

Optional gameplay function: statues become energy relays during Phase 2.

H. Lighting Specification

The reference depends on a strong warm-versus-cool contrast.

Primary directional light: low sunset from camera-left / rear-left.

Color: warm orange-gold.

Sky contribution: stormy blue-grey.

Focal light: crimson portal providing local red illumination and vertical volumetric scattering.

Secondary accent: cyan magical lights around arena and braziers.

Rim light: cool sky rim on statues, towers, and player silhouette.

Shadow density: strong but not crushed; walkable surfaces must remain readable.

Exposure: cinematic HDR, but lock auto-exposure ranges tightly enough to preserve combat readability.

Recommended UE5 systems: Directional Light, Sky Atmosphere, Sky Light, Volumetric Clouds, Exponential Height Fog with Volumetric Fog, Lumen GI/reflections, localized point/spot lights, Post Process Volume.

Wet floor reflections should help lead the eye directly to the portal.

J. Environmental Storytelling

The environment should suggest that the citadel was once a sacred transit or ascension site that has been corrupted.

Story cues:

  • Guardian statues indicate former ritual protection.
  • Broken causeway segments imply previous assaults.
  • Crimson banners identify current controlling faction.
  • Cyan runes represent the original system.
  • Crimson energy represents newly imposed power.
  • Violet fractures beneath islands imply structural corruption.
  • Broken chains suggest floating structures were once physically or magically anchored.
  • Abandoned braziers and damaged plinths can contain lore.
  • Red trees survive only near concentrated magical energy.
  • A few shattered weapons or armor fragments around the arena imply prior challengers.

Density should rise near the arena and portal, while the center of the combat space remains uncluttered.

Audio opportunities: distant bells, chain creaks, low portal resonance, wind shear, stone settling, far thunder, rune hum, crackling magical discharge.

L. Gameplay / Encounter Flow
01 — Approach

Player exits previous transition and immediately sees the citadel, portal and arena.

02 — Causeway Traversal

Broken bridge pieces teach the visual language of falling hazards and magical corruption.

03 — Outer Ring Exploration

Checkpoint and optional side route. Player can inspect statues and collect lore/reward.

04 — Arena Entry

Music drops, arena runes activate, exits seal.

05 — Boss Intro

Astral Gate Warden materializes from the central crimson line or descends from the portal dais.

06 — Boss Phase 1

Full arena available. Combat focuses on movement and understanding the boss.

07 — Boss Phase 2

Guardian statues become energy relays. Cyan rune channels pulse. Some radial sectors become temporarily unsafe.

08 — Boss Phase 3

Violet corruption fractures outer arena sections, reducing safe space while the portal intensifies.

09 — Boss Defeat

Arena returns to stable state. Crimson beam collapses briefly, then reforms as a controlled gateway.

10 — Reward / Transition

Player activates portal dais and proceeds into the citadel.

N. Collision / Navigation / Readability

Main causeway and arena should use simple blocking volumes rather than complex per-poly collision where possible.

Arena NavMesh must remain stable during Phase 1 and Phase 2.

If Phase 3 removes floor sectors, use dynamic nav modifiers only if enemies actually need to react to the change. Otherwise constrain boss movement with custom logic.

Use invisible blockers along visually impassable broken architecture where players might otherwise become stuck.

Fall edges need consistent readability: broken stones, hanging chains, mist, and stronger rim lighting.

Keep central rune lines visible during every boss phase.

P. Performance Strategy

The highest risks are not the stone geometry; they are volumetrics, translucency, dynamic lighting, VFX overdraw, distant scene complexity, and wet reflective materials.

Use Nanite aggressively for architecture and cliff detail, but simplify background silhouettes that contribute little to the frame.

Keep volumetric cloud/fog samples tuned to target platform.

Limit local shadow-casting lights around braziers.

Use emissive materials for many distant light sources rather than real lights.

Use HISM/ISM for repeated pillars, debris and background architectural fragments.

Restrict transparent particles near the camera.

Use VFX culling distances and scalability tiers.

Build distant floating islands as clustered HLODs or simplified Nanite meshes.

Avoid expensive multilayer materials on every stone asset; reserve complex wetness/corruption blends for foreground gameplay surfaces.

Use reflection quality selectively—wet ground is important, distant towers are not.

Boss-phase VFX should have explicit performance budgets.

Q. Development Roadmap
Stage 1 — Blockout

Create causeway, arena, portal dais, citadel silhouette, cliffs, boundaries and player scale.

Stage 2 — Gameplay Validation

Test movement, combat spacing, arena diameter, camera behavior, sightlines, enemy navigation and fall hazards.

Stage 3 — Structural Environment

Replace blockout with modular causeway, arena ring, stairs, pillars, arches, cliffs and major citadel architecture.

Stage 4 — Asset & Material Production

Produce portal, statues, banners, braziers, debris, red trees, PBR surfaces, wetness and corruption systems.

Stage 5 — Lighting & Atmosphere

Build sunset lighting, storm sky, cloud ocean, height fog, volumetrics, color grade and baseline VFX.

Stage 6 — Gameplay Implementation

Add boss triggers, arena barriers, rune-state logic, collapsing sections, portal activation, rewards and transitions.

Stage 7 — Optimization & Polish

Profile GPU/CPU, reduce VFX overdraw, tune Lumen and shadows, optimize background geometry, validate collision, fix visual hierarchy and finalize cinematic polish.

Final Validation Checklist
  • Reference composition preserved.
  • Citadel remains the dominant focal point.
  • Main approach axis points directly toward portal.
  • Top-down map matches visible environment.
  • Arena scale works for intended combat.
  • Player silhouette reads correctly against architecture.
  • Causeway remains navigable and readable.
  • Optional paths never confuse the main objective.
  • Background islands remain clearly non-playable.
  • Modular pieces snap correctly.
  • Hero assets use consistent material language.
  • Crimson, cyan and violet VFX retain distinct gameplay meanings.
  • Wet surfaces do not destroy gameplay readability.
  • Fog does not conceal navigation edges.
  • Boss attacks remain readable over rune VFX.
  • NavMesh remains valid during each encounter state.
  • Collision prevents snagging on decorative rubble.
  • Lumen cost is profiled on target hardware.
  • Niagara scalability is configured.
  • Background geometry uses appropriate culling/HLOD.
  • Streaming transition into the citadel is tested.
  • Final lighting matches the warm-left / cool-center reference hierarchy.
  • Final UE5 build is tested at target frame-rate and resolution.
Open Design Questions
  • PC target frame rate.
  • Third-person, first-person, or fixed cinematic camera.
  • Exact player movement speed and dodge distance.
  • Combat style and desired boss-arena duration.
  • Whether the Astral Gate Warden is humanoid, creature, or construct.
  • Whether collapsing arena sections are temporary or permanent.
  • Whether the side floating ruin is genuinely playable or only background.
  • Whether the citadel interior loads seamlessly or through a cinematic transition.
  • Whether multiplayer/co-op needs to be supported.
  • Required level completion time and expected number of regular enemies before the boss.

ENVIRONMENT 03 · UE5 PRODUCTION PLAN

Eclipsed Rootgate — Emberwood Threshold

An ancient forest sanctuary corrupted by a celestial eclipse, where a dormant gateway has reawakened beneath an unnatural crimson sky.

Primary objective: Reach the Rootgate, restore the three eclipse seals, survive the gate awakening, and cross into the next realm.

Read full production specification · 19 sections
A. Level Overview

Level Name: Eclipsed Rootgate — Emberwood Threshold

Level Category: Dark-fantasy forest traversal / ritual gateway / encounter-transition level

Theme: An ancient forest sanctuary corrupted by a celestial eclipse, where a dormant gateway has reawakened beneath an unnatural crimson sky.

Gameplay Type: Exploration → environmental traversal → light combat → ritual activation → climax encounter → portal transition

Primary Objective: Reach the Rootgate, restore the three eclipse seals, survive the gate awakening, and cross into the next realm.

Main Landmark: The glowing rectangular Rootgate built from ancient timber, roots, and ruined shrine architecture.

Secondary Landmarks: Eclipse overhead, colossal forest trunks, ember-choked clearing, mist corridors, ruined ritual posts, twisted root formations.

Intended Experience: Oppressive mystery → supernatural discovery → tension → ritual escalation → luminous release.

Visual Identity: Charcoal-black forest, wet bark, blue-grey fog, warm golden portal light, crimson eclipse glow, drifting embers, silhouetted trees.

Reference elements to preserve: giant ancient trees framing the scene, central gate silhouette, lone player scale, dense fog, black eclipse with red corona, warm portal core, cold forest shadows, suspended embers.

OBSERVED: The composition is strongly centered on a glowing gate beneath an eclipse, with the player approaching through a dark forest clearing.

INFERRED: The gateway is the natural level objective and climax.

PROPOSED: The surrounding clearing becomes an encounter/ritual space while the deeper forest supports exploration and route-building.

B. Spatial & Gameplay Specification
Overall Layout

Player Spawn → Gloomwood Trail → Fallen Shrine → Root Hollow → Eclipse Clearing → Rootgate Ritual Zone → Portal Transition

The level should preserve a strong forward visual line toward the golden gateway whenever sightlines open.

Z01 — Gloomwood Entry

Purpose: Orientation and mood establishment.

Gameplay Function: Safe traversal, tutorialized interaction, environmental storytelling.

Primary Visual Feature: Towering trunks closing around the player.

Encounter Type: None or minimal ambient threat.

Traversal: Ground path, shallow roots, low elevation changes.

Z02 — Mistwood Descent

Purpose: Break direct sightline and make the gate feel remote.

Gameplay Function: Navigation and first enemy contact.

Visual Feature: Dense volumetric fog between black tree trunks.

Encounter: Small roaming forest-corrupted enemies.

Traversal: Sloped path, fallen logs, root steps.

Z03 — Fallen Shrine

Purpose: Introduce the gate’s history and the first eclipse seal.

Gameplay Function: Exploration, lore, optional reward.

Visual Feature: Broken timber-and-stone ritual structure.

Encounter: Small ambush or environmental hazard.

Traversal: Tight ruin spaces opening into forest.

Z04 — Root Hollow

Purpose: Mid-level traversal challenge.

Gameplay Function: Climb-over / under-root movement, light platforming, second seal.

Visual Feature: Interlocked roots and hollow trunk chambers.

Encounter: Elite guardian or environmental corruption.

Traversal: Vertical root ramps, narrow passages, natural bridges.

Z05 — Eclipse Clearing

Purpose: Major reveal of the full eclipse and Rootgate.

Gameplay Function: Checkpoint, preparation, optional third-seal path.

Visual Feature: Wide clearing framed by monumental trees.

Encounter: None before activation; high tension only.

Traversal: Broad readable ground plane.

Z06 — Rootgate Ritual Zone

Purpose: Main objective and encounter climax.

Gameplay Function: Activate gate, defend ritual, defeat Warden if used.

Visual Feature: Golden portal inside rough ancient gate architecture.

Encounter: Multi-wave ritual defense or boss encounter.

Traversal: Circular/semicircular arena movement around gateway.

Z07 — Beyond the Gate

Purpose: Transition.

Gameplay Function: Reward and streaming handoff.

Visual Feature: Overexposed golden interior with silhouette hints of the next realm.

Encounter: None.

Primary Route

A readable but not perfectly straight forest path. The Rootgate is visible early, hidden through the middle third, then fully revealed again at the Eclipse Clearing.

Secondary Route

A side trail through the Fallen Shrine leading to lore, upgrade material, or a seal shortcut.

Optional Route

A root canopy or elevated trunk path giving a temporary view above the fog and rewarding exploration.

Secret Area

A hollow beneath a root mass containing a relic tied to the former gatekeepers.

Checkpoints
  • CP01 — Fallen Shrine
  • CP02 — Eclipse Clearing
  • CP03 — Post-encounter gate activation

Playable Boundaries

Dense root walls, impassable tree trunks, deep fog ravines, thorn corruption, and steep terrain should form natural boundaries instead of obvious invisible walls.

Background-Only Space

Distant forest silhouettes, far canopy layers, eclipse sky, and off-path giant trunks should remain non-playable.

E. Hero Asset Specifications
HA-01 — Eclipsed Rootgate

Purpose: Primary objective, visual climax, level transition.

Placement: Center of the final clearing.

Proposed Scale: 24–28 m overall height, 10 m portal width.

Mesh Type: Nanite static architecture with separate animated energy elements.

Collision: Simplified box/convex collision; portal interior uses trigger volume.

Interaction: Locked until all seals are activated.

Animation: Root movement, timber flex, rune glow, energy surge.

Destruction: Optional surface cracking only; no full collapse required.

Materials: Burned timber, wet root bark, aged stone, glowing gold energy.

VFX: Sparks, ember bloom, falling ash, distortion, god rays, volumetric light.

Reuse: Unique.

HA-02 — Ancient Guardian Tree

Purpose: Establish monumental scale and frame composition.

Placement: Foreground left/right and deeper midground.

Scale: 50–80 m height.

Implementation: Nanite hero tree mesh plus reusable branch/root sub-kit.

Collision: Simplified trunk/root collision near playable space only.

Reuse: 3–5 silhouette variants.

HA-03 — Eclipse

Purpose: Global identity, lighting justification, narrative state indicator.

Implementation: Sky material / distant celestial mesh, animated corona, cloud interaction.

Gameplay: Can intensify during ritual phases through an MPC.

H. Lighting Specification

The lighting must preserve the reference’s cold forest / warm portal / crimson sky separation.

Primary Light: Weak eclipse-muted directional light from above/front.

Key Light: Soft cool-grey environment illumination.

Fill: Very low cool ambient fill from sky and mist.

Focal Light: Strong warm golden light from inside the Rootgate.

Rim Light: Crimson-pink eclipse rim along tree silhouettes and fog edges.

Shadow Density: High; foreground trunks can approach silhouette.

Exposure: Controlled cinematic exposure with portal highlights protected from clipping.

Color Contrast: blue-grey/charcoal environment vs gold/orange portal vs crimson eclipse.

Fog Relationship: Portal light should scatter heavily through near-ground fog.

Emissive Contribution: Gate and embers provide local warm bounce.

Recommended UE5 systems:

  • Directional Light
  • Sky Light
  • Sky Atmosphere
  • Exponential Height Fog
  • Volumetric Fog
  • Volumetric Clouds
  • Lumen
  • Point/Rect Lights near the gate
  • Post Process Volume

J. Environmental Storytelling

The forest should imply that the Rootgate predates the current civilization and was once maintained by a forgotten order.

Suggested clues:

  • shrine fragments swallowed by roots;
  • carved seal stones split by pressure from tree growth;
  • burnt ritual stakes around the gateway;
  • offerings trapped beneath leaf litter;
  • dead hanging charms;
  • claw or weapon marks in timber;
  • old lantern hooks with no lamps;
  • patches of vitrified soil near the gate;
  • skeletal branch growth pointing toward the eclipse;
  • embers appearing only inside the gate’s influence radius.

Story density should increase toward the gate, while the main traversal lane stays visually clean.

Audio opportunities: wind through canopy, distant tree groans, insects fading as the eclipse intensifies, ember crackle, low portal resonance, root creaks, ritual whispers, sub-bass eclipse rumble.

L. Gameplay / Encounter Flow
01 — Entry

Player enters the forest under the eclipse; the distant gate glow is visible between trees.

02 — First Descent

The path narrows into fog; minor enemies establish danger.

03 — First Seal

The player reaches the Fallen Shrine and activates Seal 01.

04 — Root Hollow

Traversal becomes more vertical and claustrophobic. Seal 02 lies inside the root formation.

05 — Optional Discovery

A side route offers lore/reward and a view over the clearing.

06 — Eclipse Clearing

The environment opens dramatically; the player sees the full gate and eclipse.

07 — Final Seal

Seal 03 activates the Rootgate and changes the lighting/VFX state.

08 — Encounter Initiation

Roots move, embers intensify, exits temporarily close.

09 — Main Encounter

Preferred structure: ritual defense against corrupted gate guardians, or a single Eclipse Warden if a boss is desired.

10 — Climax

Portal reaches maximum gold intensity while the eclipse corona shifts brighter red.

11 — Defeat / Stabilization

Enemies vanish, mist recedes locally, gate stabilizes.

12 — Reward / Exit

Player collects a relic and enters the portal.

P. Performance Strategy

The biggest likely costs are volumetric fog, translucent ember effects, dense foliage/tree overdraw, Lumen in heavily occluded spaces, shadowed giant trees, and the glowing portal.

Use Nanite for high-detail tree trunks, roots, rock, and shrine assets.

Use HISM/ISM for repeated background trees and small props.

Use PCG only for background/secondary forest distribution where art-direction control is not critical.

Keep foreground hero trees hand-placed.

Cull tiny ember/ash particles aggressively with distance.

Reserve shadow-casting local lights for the gate and a very small number of ritual props.

Use emissive materials instead of physical lights for distant warm specks.

Reduce volumetric fog quality in lower scalability tiers.

Use simplified collision for complex roots and giant trunks.

Avoid high-cost subsurface foliage everywhere; reserve it for canopy edges that receive visible eclipse light.

Profile the portal bloom and translucent particles during ritual climax, when the scene is most expensive.

Q. Development Roadmap
Stage 1 — Blockout

Build forest footprint, route, clearing, gate, ravines, hero tree masses, and player scale.

Stage 2 — Gameplay Validation

Validate traversal width, route readability, gate reveal timing, encounter area size, enemy navigation, and checkpoint placement.

Stage 3 — Structural Environment

Produce roots, hero trees, shrine pieces, terrain banks, clearing, and Rootgate blockout replacement.

Stage 4 — Asset & Material Production

Finalize bark, roots, soil, ruins, ritual props, seal stones, gate, decals, and environmental variants.

Stage 5 — Lighting & Atmosphere

Implement eclipse sky, directional lighting, fog, cloud state, portal light, ember field, and final color grade.

Stage 6 — Gameplay Implementation

Add seal logic, barriers, encounter controller, corruption hazards, rewards, portal state changes, and level transition.

Stage 7 — Optimization & Polish

Profile Nanite, Lumen, foliage, Niagara, volumetric fog, shadows, collision, NavMesh, streaming, and final cinematic readability.

Final Validation Checklist
  • Eclipse composition matches the reference mood.
  • Rootgate remains the dominant focal point.
  • Player silhouette reads clearly at the gate.
  • Forest scale feels monumental rather than ordinary.
  • Golden portal remains distinct from the crimson eclipse.
  • Main route remains readable in dense fog.
  • Background trees never imply false traversal routes.
  • Hero tree placement frames rather than hides the objective.
  • Root and shrine kits snap cleanly.
  • Seal locations are readable without UI dependence.
  • Ritual VFX do not hide enemy silhouettes.
  • Fog does not obscure dangerous ledges.
  • Portal bloom remains controlled.
  • NavMesh is valid before and during encounter states.
  • Collision does not snag the player on decorative roots.
  • Background forest uses appropriate HISM/HLOD/culling.
  • Niagara systems have scalability tiers.
  • Lumen and volumetrics are profiled on target hardware.
  • Portal transition streams correctly.
  • Final environment, map, dimensions, assets, and gameplay all describe the same level.
Open Design Questions
  • PC target frame rate.
  • Third-person or first-person camera.
  • Whether the final encounter is a boss, ritual defense, or environmental survival sequence.
  • Exact level duration.
  • Whether climbing or mantle traversal is supported.
  • Whether destructible roots or shrine pieces are required.
  • Whether the Rootgate is a seamless level-streaming portal or a cinematic load transition.
  • Whether multiplayer/co-op must be supported.
  • Whether the eclipse state changes globally after completion.
  • Whether the forest is a standalone level or part of a larger open-world biome.

OBSERVED: the environment is extremely sparse, nearly colorless, and built around one dominant circular red focal point framed by dead trees.

INFERRED: the circular formation naturally reads as the level objective and boss/transition arena.

PROPOSED: the surrounding barren plain becomes a readable combat/traversal field with environmental hazards created by fissures, corrupted roots, and unstable red energy.

B. Spatial & Gameplay Specification
Overall Layout

Spawn Ridge → Fractured Plain → Shard Field → Root Scar → Threshold Basin → Scarlet Root Ring → Beyond the Veil

The level should use long sightlines. Unlike the previous dense forest environment, this one should feel exposed and psychologically unsafe.

Z01 — Ashen Spawn Ridge

Purpose: Establish scale and immediately reveal the Root Ring.

Gameplay Function: Safe orientation space.

Primary Feature: Distant portal centered on horizon.

Encounter: None.

Traversal: Gentle descent.

Z02 — Fractured Plain

Purpose: Long approach and environmental storytelling.

Gameplay Function: Basic traversal and first enemies.

Primary Feature: Cracked pale terrain with black fissures.

Encounter: Small roaming enemies.

Traversal: Open ground with fractured surface obstacles.

Z03 — Shard Field

Purpose: Break the open space with combat cover and navigation choices.

Gameplay Function: Medium combat zone / optional loot.

Primary Feature: Angular black rock slabs and toppled monolith fragments.

Encounter: Regular enemy groups.

Traversal: Weaving between stone debris.

Z04 — Root Scar

Purpose: First major supernatural escalation.

Gameplay Function: Hazard traversal.

Primary Feature: Black roots emerging from terrain with crimson internal glow.

Encounter: Corrupted enemies / environmental damage zones.

Traversal: Narrow safe lanes across fissures.

Z05 — Threshold Basin

Purpose: Pre-boss staging area and checkpoint.

Gameplay Function: Preparation, optional lore, final approach.

Primary Feature: Broad flat area beneath the giant dead trees.

Encounter: Optional elite guardian.

Traversal: Open movement.

Z06 — Scarlet Root Ring Arena

Purpose: Main climax.

Gameplay Function: Boss encounter and ritual activation.

Primary Feature: Red circular portal embraced by gigantic dead tree trunks.

Encounter: Warden of the Threshold.

Traversal: Large circular combat field with clear radial lanes.

Z07 — Beyond the Veil

Purpose: Level transition.

Gameplay Function: Post-boss reward and streaming handoff.

Primary Feature: Crimson fog and distorted terrain beyond the gateway.

Encounter: None.

Primary Route

A mostly direct line from spawn toward the Root Ring. The portal should remain visible through almost the entire level.

Secondary Route

A curved route through the Shard Field containing combat cover and lore fragments.

Optional Route

A cracked ridge on the left flank leading to a high viewpoint and reward.

Secret Area

A collapsed fissure cavity beneath one of the giant root masses, containing a rare relic.

Checkpoints
  • CP01 — Shard Field edge
  • CP02 — Threshold Basin
  • CP03 — Post-boss gateway

Playable Boundaries

Use raised black ridges, impassable fissures, root walls, steep drops, and storm-obscured distance instead of obvious invisible walls.

Background Scenery

Distant mountains, cloud walls, secondary dead trees, and far-off black silhouettes are background-only.

E. Hero Asset Specifications
HA-01 — Scarlet Root Ring

Purpose: Primary landmark, final objective, boss arena anchor, and level-transition device.

Placement: Horizon-center throughout the entire level.

Proposed Scale: 55 m outer diameter; approximately 35 m inner opening.

Mesh Type: Two or more giant Nanite root-tree meshes forming the structural ring, supplemented by modular roots.

Collision: Simplified trunk/root blockers; portal opening uses trigger volume.

Interaction: Dormant before ritual completion; fully active after boss defeat.

Animation: Subtle root movement, vein pulsing, bark splitting, energy buildup.

Destruction: Limited surface fracture only. Core silhouette must remain intact.

Materials: Near-black carbonized bark with controlled crimson emissive channels.

VFX: Energy ring, heat distortion, red fog, sparks, floating ash, lightning-like arcs.

Reuse: Unique.

HA-02 / HA-03 — Root Titan Trees

Purpose: Create the iconic arch around the portal and communicate impossible scale.

Implementation: High-detail Nanite sculpts with modular branch/root additions.

Variants: Left-dominant, right-dominant, broken-spire, split-trunk.

Collision: Only on surfaces the player can physically reach.

HA-04 — Threshold Ground Sigil

A subtle circular or radial cracked-stone pattern beneath the Root Ring.

During the boss fight, emissive lines can activate without changing the original overall environment identity.

H. Lighting Specification

This environment depends on near-monochrome values with highly selective red illumination.

Fill: Very limited.

Focal Light: Saturated red from the Root Ring.

Shadow Density: High-contrast but readable.

Exposure: Slightly underexposed environment with protected red emissive highlights.

Color Contrast: 90% grey/black/white, 10% crimson.

Fog: Light atmospheric haze only; do not obscure the strong graphic silhouette.

J. Environmental Storytelling

The environment should imply that this region was once fertile but was sterilized by the Root Ring’s activation.

Story clues:

  • Dead roots radiate away from the gateway.
  • Cracks become denser toward the arena.
  • Some stone shards appear fused or vitrified.
  • No healthy vegetation exists.
  • Occasional dead shrubs become fully black near corruption zones.
  • Old ritual fragments can be half-buried beneath ash.
  • Root growth has pierced former structures.
  • The portal’s red light permanently stains nearby surfaces.
  • Broken weapons around the basin imply previous failed challengers.
  • Distant ridges suggest the corruption extends far beyond the playable space.

Audio opportunities:

low-frequency wind, distant thunder, dry ground movement, root creaks, faint energy hum, stone grinding, ash hiss, portal resonance, and silence drops before boss phases.

Player spawns with the Root Ring immediately visible.

02 — Long Approach

Sparse enemies and huge negative space establish vulnerability.

First meaningful combat encounter among broken black rocks.

Full arena available.

Root eruptions divide the arena into temporary lanes.

Crimson fissures expand and selected ground sectors become dangerous.

13 — Reward / Exit

Player claims a relic and enters the Root Ring.

N. Collision / Navigation / Gameplay Readability

Keep the enormous central arena surface clean and predictable.

Use simplified collision on root masses and angular rocks.

Do not allow small decorative cracks to snag player movement.

Large fissures must use consistent visual telegraphing before they become lethal.

Boss NavMesh should remain fully valid during Phase 1.

For Phase 2–3, prefer Nav Modifier Volumes over rebuilding complex navigation at runtime unless necessary.

Use red ground illumination only for dangerous/interactive states, so the accent color maintains gameplay meaning.

The black Root Ring silhouette must remain readable against the pale storm sky at all camera angles.

P. Performance Strategy

Primary performance risks:

  • enormous Nanite root silhouettes,
  • wide-screen shadow coverage,
  • volumetric storm clouds,
  • intense emissive portal,
  • transparent crimson VFX,
  • Lumen bounce from the gateway,
  • large boss arena,
  • distant rock/terrain geometry.

Optimization strategy:

Use Nanite for hero root-trees and rocks, but avoid unnecessarily dense unseen underside geometry.

Use HISM/ISM for repeated debris.

Use aggressive culling for small black shards beyond gameplay distance.

Keep portal VFX mostly mesh-based where possible rather than stacking many transparent sprites.

Use emissive contribution carefully so the portal does not create excessive Lumen noise.

Keep only a few dynamic shadow-casting local lights.

Use HLOD for distant ridge lines and background root silhouettes.

Use material instances rather than unique shaders for terrain variations.

Reduce particle density during combat-heavy boss phases.

Provide VFX scalability tiers.

Profile the scene specifically at the point where Phase 3 hazards, boss VFX, cloud lightning, and portal effects overlap.

Q. Development Roadmap
Stage 1 — Blockout

Create terrain footprint, portal silhouette, arena, fissures, spawn, boundaries, and player scale.

Stage 2 — Gameplay Validation

Test approach duration, boss spacing, route readability, sightlines, camera behavior, hazard width, and navigation.

Stage 3 — Structural Environment

Replace blockout with root titans, rock shards, terrain ridges, cracked ground, and portal geometry.

Stage 4 — Asset & Material Production

Create root sculpts, rock variants, terrain blends, corrupted materials, props, decals, and hero portal.

Stage 5 — Lighting & Atmosphere

Build storm sky, pale diffuse light, crimson portal light, cloud contrast, ash atmosphere, and monochrome grade.

Stage 6 — Gameplay Implementation

Add seals, arena trigger, root barriers, boss events, fissure hazards, phase transitions, rewards, and portal travel.

Stage 7 — Optimization & Polish

Profile CPU/GPU, Nanite, Lumen, VFX, shadows, volumetrics, streaming, NavMesh, collision, and final art polish.

Q. Final Validation Checklist
  • Reference silhouette preserved.
  • Root Ring remains centered and dominant.
  • Player scale communicates monumental environment size.
  • Palette remains predominantly monochrome.
  • Crimson remains the only major saturated accent.
  • Portal is visible from spawn.
  • Main route is readable despite sparse landmarks.
  • Background mountains remain non-playable.
  • Arena dimensions support combat.
  • Root tree geometry remains consistent across views.
  • Hero environment and top-down map match.
  • Fissures communicate danger before damage.
  • Boss attacks remain readable over red VFX.
  • Nanite cost is profiled.
  • Lumen noise near the portal is controlled.
  • Volumetric clouds remain performant.
  • Niagara systems use culling/scalability.
  • HISM/ISM is used for repeated debris.
  • Collision avoids snagging.
  • NavMesh works through all phases.
  • Streaming transition through the portal is verified.
  • Final UE5 build matches the black/white/red reference hierarchy.
Open Design Questions
  • PC target frame rate.
  • Third-person or first-person camera.
  • Exact combat system and dodge/mobility range.
  • Whether the final encounter is a single boss or boss + adds.
  • Desired level duration.
  • Whether the ground can permanently collapse during the boss fight.
  • Whether traversal includes jumping, mantling, or climbing.
  • Whether multiplayer/co-op must be supported.
  • Whether the area is standalone or connected to a larger world.
  • Whether portal travel is seamless streaming or a cinematic loading transition.

B. Spatial & Gameplay Specification
Overall Layout

Z01 Ashen Arrival → Z02 Skull Causeway → Z03 Horned Ossuary → Z04 Infernal Courtyard → Z05 Seal Bastions → Z06 Maw Gate Arena → Z07 Citadel Interior Transition

The level should retain an extremely strong centerline. The player should almost always understand that the fortress mouth is the destination.

Z01 — Ashen Arrival

Purpose: Establish the citadel, moon, and impossible scale.

Gameplay Function: Safe orientation and narrative setup.

Primary Visual Feature: Full silhouette of the fortress and moon.

Encounter Type: None.

Traversal: Broad flat approach.

Z02 — Skull Causeway

Purpose: Begin hostile traversal.

Gameplay Function: First combat waves and hazard introduction.

Primary Visual Feature: Black stone path framed by demonic skull piles.

Encounter Type: Common enemies plus ranged threats.

Traversal: Ground combat with scattered debris cover.

Z03 — Horned Ossuary

Purpose: Increase environmental density and introduce optional exploration.

Gameplay Function: Elite encounter, lore pickup, optional reward.

Primary Visual Feature: Giant skulls, broken horns, bone mounds, ritual remains.

Encounter Type: Elite demon / corrupted knight equivalent.

Traversal: Slight lateral branching.

Z04 — Infernal Courtyard

Purpose: Give the player a wider battlefield directly before the gate.

Gameplay Function: Multi-directional combat and seal interaction.

Primary Visual Feature: Fortress walls, side towers, lava-red fissures, banners or chained relics.

Encounter Type: Mixed enemy wave.

Traversal: Open combat space with radial movement.

Z05 — Seal Bastions

Three seal points positioned around the courtyard.

Purpose: Gate progression.

Gameplay Function: Activate/destroy seals to weaken the Maw Gate.

Primary Visual Feature: Demonic obelisks or horned altars.

Encounter Type: Guarded interaction points.

Traversal: Left, right, and center route decisions.

Z06 — Maw Gate Arena

Purpose: Main boss/climax zone.

Gameplay Function: Boss encounter plus portal activation.

Primary Visual Feature: Tooth-lined gate mouth opening into crimson darkness.

Encounter Type: Maw Warden boss.

Traversal: Wide semicircular arena with strong frontal readability.

Z07 — Citadel Interior Transition

Purpose: Level handoff.

Gameplay Function: Short post-boss walk and streaming transition.

Primary Visual Feature: Dark interior corridor with pulsating red architectural veins.

Encounter Type: None.

Routes

Primary Route: straight central causeway.

Secondary Route: two side loops through skull fields connecting back to the courtyard.

Optional Route: elevated debris ledge or ruined side platform containing loot/lore.

Secret Area: cavity beneath a giant skull cluster accessible after breaking a bone wall.

Checkpoint 01: end of Skull Causeway.

Checkpoint 02: Infernal Courtyard.

Checkpoint 03: post-boss gate interior.

Playable Boundaries

Use skull banks, horn spikes, fortress walls, deep red chasms, impassable debris, and burning fissures.

Avoid obvious invisible walls where geometry can communicate the boundary naturally.

E. Hero Asset Specifications
HA-01 — Devouring Citadel

Purpose: Primary environmental identity and permanent visual target.

Placement: Dead center on the level’s main axis.

Scale: approximately 140–180 m facade width and 120–160 m visible height.

Construction: modular black fortress modules assembled into one unique horned silhouette.

Mesh Type: Nanite static meshes.

Collision: simplified architectural collision only in accessible lower sections.

Interaction: none for most facade geometry.

Destruction: localized damage only.

Materials: black iron, volcanic stone, charred bone ornament, subtle crimson emissive channels.

VFX: smoke, falling embers, red atmospheric haze.

HA-02 — Maw Gate

Purpose: level objective, boss focal point, and transition.

Placement: exact center of citadel facade.

Scale: approximately 28 m wide × 36 m high.

Design: architectural mouth with large white-black teeth and a deep red interior.

Interaction: sealed initially; opens after three seals and boss completion.

Animation: jaw/teeth movement, breathing motion, gate distortion, energy buildup.

Collision: gate blocker before unlock; transition trigger afterward.

VFX: red vapor, heat distortion, sparks, inner glow, shockwave.

Reuse: unique.

HA-03 — Bloodmoon

Purpose: sky landmark and primary lighting narrative.

Implementation: large sky sphere/material element rather than physical near-world geometry.

Surface: molten red/orange/yellow patterns.

Animation: extremely slow surface turbulence.

Gameplay Link: corona intensity can rise as seals are broken.

HA-04 — Giant Demon Skull

Purpose: frame the approach and communicate past devastation.

Reuse: create one master sculpt with 4–6 horn, jaw, damage, and orientation variants.

Collision: simplified only where reachable.

H. Lighting Specification

The composition should preserve the reference’s overpowering red atmospheric dominance while ensuring the fortress remains readable as a black silhouette.

Primary Light: bloodmoon-driven warm directional light.

Key Direction: rear/top-center, aligned broadly behind the fortress.

Fill: weak red ambient skylight.

Rim Light: strong red/orange rim on fortress horns and skulls.

Focal Light: deep crimson inside the Maw Gate.

Accent: occasional white-hot/yellow highlights from the bloodmoon.

Shadow Density: very high.

Exposure: lock exposure tightly; prevent the moon from flattening the foreground into pure black.

Color Hierarchy:

  • black/charcoal architecture;
  • saturated crimson atmosphere;
  • orange-yellow celestial highlights;
  • pale teeth/bone contrast.

UE5 systems:

  • Directional Light
  • Sky Light
  • Sky Atmosphere
  • Volumetric Clouds
  • Exponential Height Fog
  • Volumetric Fog
  • Lumen
  • Point/Rect Lights around gate
  • Post Process Volume

J. Environmental Storytelling

The citadel should imply that it was not simply constructed; it was grown, forged, and fed.

Environmental clues:

  • skulls become larger closer to the fortress;
  • some skulls are fused directly into walls;
  • broken horns form ceremonial boundary markers;
  • tooth fragments lie near the gate;
  • chains disappear into inaccessible pits;
  • scorch patterns radiate outward from seal bastions;
  • red veins in the floor converge on the gate;
  • failed siege equipment can appear half-melted into terrain;
  • crushed armor establishes scale of previous battles;
  • giant skulls suggest extinct titan-class demons or victims.

Density should increase toward the fortress while the playable center lane remains clear.

Audio opportunities: distant roars, grinding stone, chain tension, low breathing from the gate, heavy wind, thunder, fire crackle, sub-bass moon resonance, metallic groans.

L. Gameplay / Encounter Flow
01 — Arrival

The entire citadel and bloodmoon are revealed immediately.

02 — Causeway Advance

Small enemies establish movement and combat rhythm.

03 — Ossuary Ambush

Large skull clusters create cover and flank routes.

04 — First Seal

Player destroys or activates Seal A.

05 — Courtyard Battle

Enemy density increases; fortress architecture dominates the frame.

06 — Side Seal Routes

Player clears left and right bastions.

07 — Maw Awakening

The gate becomes animated; teeth move, inner darkness glows, environmental audio changes.

08 — Boss Intro

The Maw Warden emerges from the mouth or descends from the facade.

09 — Boss Phase 1

Full arena available; standard melee/ranged pattern.

10 — Boss Phase 2

Ground fissures activate and divide the arena.

11 — Boss Phase 3

Bloodmoon brightness spikes; sections of the fortress pulse with red energy; gate begins opening behind the boss.

12 — Boss Defeat

Arena VFX rapidly collapse toward the gate.

13 — Gate Opening

The Maw stretches open, revealing a dark-red interior passage.

14 — Reward / Transition

Player receives a progression item and enters the citadel.

N. Collision / Navigation / Gameplay Readability

Keep the central causeway and boss arena collision extremely clean.

Use simplified convex collision for skulls and horn structures.

Decorative teeth near the gate should not create tiny snagging gaps.

NavMesh should support flank routes through the Ossuary and full arena movement.

Boss-phase hazards should use Nav Modifier Volumes only when AI needs to respond.

The pale gate teeth must stay readable against the dark architecture.

Use brighter red floor telegraphs only for actual danger states so players can distinguish ambient crimson from gameplay crimson.

P. Performance Strategy

Likely major costs:

  • enormous fortress Nanite density;
  • large bloodmoon sky effect;
  • high-intensity emissive red lighting;
  • volumetric clouds/fog;
  • heavy translucent ash and ember VFX;
  • dynamic boss effects;
  • shadowed skull fields;
  • complex tooth/gate silhouette;
  • distant fortress towers.

Recommended mitigation:

Use Nanite aggressively for fortress, skulls, and rubble, but simplify unseen rear geometry.

Use HISM/ISM for bone piles, spikes, rubble, and small architectural repeats.

Keep the bloodmoon mostly material-driven instead of particle-heavy.

Use mesh particles for distant embers where practical.

Restrict shadow-casting point lights.

Clamp emissive contribution where Lumen becomes noisy.

Use VFX culling and scalability tiers.

Use HLODs for peripheral fortress towers.

Profile the boss arena during Phase 3, when moon corona, fissure VFX, boss attacks, gate animation, fog, and particles overlap.

Q. Development Roadmap
Stage 1 — Blockout

Causeway, courtyard, seal positions, gate, fortress massing, arena, player scale.

Stage 2 — Gameplay Validation

Combat spacing, route clarity, arena width, seal flow, boss camera, NavMesh.

Stage 3 — Structural Environment

Modular walls, towers, spikes, gate, skull fields, side architecture.

Stage 4 — Asset & Material Production

Hero skulls, gate teeth, props, bones, fortress materials, emissive corruption.

Stage 5 — Lighting & Atmosphere

Bloodmoon sky, red ambient light, volumetric haze, shadows, post-process grade.

Stage 6 — Gameplay Implementation

Seals, waves, arena barriers, hazards, boss logic, gate activation, transition.

Stage 7 — Optimization & Polish

CPU/GPU profiling, Nanite, Lumen, VFX, shadows, collision, streaming, cinematics, final art pass.

R. Final Validation Checklist

  • Citadel remains centered beneath the bloodmoon.
  • Moon-to-fortress scale relationship is preserved.
  • Maw Gate remains the central objective.
  • Giant skulls frame rather than block the causeway.
  • Palette remains predominantly black + crimson + molten gold.
  • Causeway is readable from spawn.
  • Gameplay spaces remain clear despite dense peripheral detail.
  • Hero facade matches all camera views and map diagrams.
  • Seal locations agree with the gameplay-flow map.
  • Boss arena supports intended movement.
  • Gate animation does not break collision.
  • Pale teeth remain readable during heavy VFX.
  • Hazard red is distinguishable from ambient red.
  • NavMesh remains valid through all encounter phases.
  • Nanite cost is profiled.
  • Lumen noise is controlled.
  • Volumetric clouds/fog meet target performance.
  • Niagara systems use culling and scalability.
  • Distant towers use HLOD/culling.
  • Streaming transition into the citadel is verified.
  • Final UE5 lighting matches the reference’s extreme red-black hierarchy.
Open Design Questions
  • PC target frame rate.
  • Third-person, first-person, or cinematic camera.
  • Exact combat system and player mobility.
  • Whether the Maw Warden is humanoid, beast, construct, or living piece of the fortress.
  • Desired level duration.
  • Whether seal objectives can be completed in any order.
  • Whether skull/bone cover is destructible.
  • Whether boss arena destruction persists after combat.
  • Whether multiplayer/co-op must be supported.
  • Whether entering the Maw Gate uses seamless streaming or a cinematic level transition.

ENVIRONMENT 06 · UE5 PRODUCTION PLAN

The Hollow Eclipse — Valley of the Black Sun

A drowned valley frozen beneath a permanent eclipse, where a dead fortress and an ancient world-tree frame a celestial anomaly

Primary objective: Cross the flooded valley, restore three eclipse beacons, reach the central eclipse basin, defeat the Hollow Sentinel, and open the path beyond the black sun

A. Level Overview
ItemProduction Definition
Level NameThe Hollow Eclipse — Valley of the Black Sun
Level CategoryOpen dark-fantasy valley / ruined stronghold approach / eclipse ritual zone
ThemeA drowned valley frozen beneath a permanent eclipse, where a dead fortress and an ancient world-tree frame a celestial anomaly
Gameplay TypeExploration → wetland traversal → ruined-fortress combat → ritual investigation → eclipse climax → level transition
Primary ObjectiveCross the flooded valley, restore three eclipse beacons, reach the central eclipse basin, defeat the Hollow Sentinel, and open the path beyond the black sun
Main LandmarkGiant black eclipse with brilliant white corona dominating the center horizon
Secondary LandmarksRuined spired fortress on the left ridge, giant twisted tree on the right ridge, reflective basin, mountain wall, drowned tree line
Intended ExperienceSilence → awe → unease → isolation → occult discovery → cosmic confrontation
Visual IdentityNearly monochrome charcoal/black/grey world with high-value white eclipse light and subtle cold silver reflections
Reference Elements to PreserveCentral eclipse, left fortress silhouette, right hero tree, low wet basin, mountain valley, storm sky, mist, sparse dead vegetation, high-contrast grayscale

OBSERVED: the composition is strongly divided between a fortress mass on the left and an ancient tree mass on the right, both framing the central eclipse.

INFERRED: the flat reflective basin is the natural traversal corridor and final encounter staging space.

PROPOSED: the eclipse basin becomes the level climax, while the fortress and tree act as two secondary objectives that unlock access to the central ritual zone.

B. Spatial & Gameplay Specification
Overall Layout

Z01 Drowned Shore → Z02 Mirror Marsh → Z03 Black Spire Ruins → Z04 Rootwatch Ridge → Z05 Eclipse Basin → Z06 Hollow Sentinel Arena → Z07 Veil Passage

The level should preserve long sightlines. The eclipse should remain visible from most major spaces and continuously orient the player.

Z01 — Drowned Shore

Purpose: Introduce the valley and full landmark hierarchy.

Gameplay Function: Safe orientation and movement introduction.

Primary Visual Feature: Eclipse centered between fortress and giant tree.

Encounter Type: None.

Traversal: Shallow water, mud, low rock shelves.

Z02 — Mirror Marsh

Purpose: Slow the player and emphasize reflection, scale, and silence.

Gameplay Function: Exploration, first threats, environmental storytelling.

Primary Feature: Dark reflective water broken by dead trees and stone fragments.

Encounter: Small wandering enemies or shadow apparitions.

Traversal: Shallow water, stepping stones, fallen branches, narrow dry paths.

Z03 — Black Spire Ruins

Purpose: First major gameplay objective.

Gameplay Function: Combat, beacon activation, elevated viewpoint.

Primary Feature: Ruined gothic silhouette on the left ridge.

Encounter: Elite enemy group / mini-boss guardian.

Traversal: Broken stairs, terraces, collapsed corridors.

Z04 — Rootwatch Ridge

Purpose: Counterbalance the fortress with a natural occult objective.

Gameplay Function: Exploration, ritual interaction, optional lore.

Primary Feature: Massive twisted dead tree overlooking the basin.

Encounter: Environmental hazard or spectral guardian.

Traversal: Root ramps, sloped rock path, narrow ridge.

Z05 — Eclipse Basin

Purpose: Bring both objective routes back together.

Gameplay Function: Checkpoint, preparation, final reveal.

Primary Feature: Broad reflective basin directly beneath the eclipse.

Encounter: None before ritual completion.

Traversal: Open ground and shallow water.

Z06 — Hollow Sentinel Arena

Purpose: Main climax.

Gameplay Function: Boss encounter and eclipse activation.

Primary Feature: White corona reflected on black water.

Encounter: Hollow Sentinel boss.

Traversal: Large circular arena with shallow-water movement.

Z07 — Veil Passage

Purpose: Transition to next level.

Gameplay Function: Post-boss reward and streaming handoff.

Primary Feature: Eclipse light collapses into a vertical silver path or portal over the water.

Encounter: None.

Route Structure

Primary Route: Drowned Shore → Mirror Marsh → Eclipse Basin.

Fortress Route: Mirror Marsh → Black Spire Ruins → Beacon 01 → return to Basin.

Tree Route: Mirror Marsh → Rootwatch Ridge → Beacon 02 → return to Basin.

Final Beacon: placed at the edge of the central basin or under a drowned shrine.

Optional Route: submerged ruin cluster containing lore and upgrade material.

Secret Area: hidden below the roots of the giant tree or behind collapsed masonry inside the fortress.

Checkpoints:

CP01 — Mirror Marsh edge

CP02 — Black Spire / Rootwatch midpoint

CP03 — Eclipse Basin before boss

CP04 — Post-boss transition

J. Environmental Storytelling

The valley should imply that the fortress and tree were once opposing guardians of the eclipse basin.

Environmental clues:

  • fortress stonework contains celestial motifs;
  • dead roots point toward the eclipse basin;
  • drowned statues face the same central point;
  • old causeway stones disappear beneath the marsh;
  • cracked beacon pedestals imply failed rituals;
  • abandoned equipment near the fortress suggests a final defense;
  • the giant tree has ritual bindings or carved marks;
  • water around the basin reflects the eclipse unnaturally clearly;
  • dead trees thin out near the exact arena center;
  • cloud motion subtly spirals around the eclipse.

Audio opportunities: distant thunder, shallow-water footsteps, wet wind, tree creaks, echoing stone, faint celestial hum, intermittent birdless silence, low-frequency eclipse resonance.

L. Gameplay / Encounter Flow
01 — Valley Reveal

The eclipse, fortress, tree, and basin are all visible immediately.

02 — Mirror Marsh

Player learns wetland traversal and encounters first threats.

03 — Route Choice

Player can approach the fortress or Rootwatch Ridge first.

04 — Fortress Objective

Combat through broken terraces and activate Beacon 01.

05 — Tree Objective

Traverse roots and activate Beacon 02.

06 — Drowned Shrine

Return to central lowland and activate Beacon 03.

07 — Eclipse Basin Opens

Silver-white light intensifies and the water becomes unnaturally still.

08 — Boss Intro

The Hollow Sentinel rises from the basin or emerges from a reflected version of the eclipse.

09 — Phase 1

Full arena open; shallow water supports readable movement.

10 — Phase 2

Concentric water shockwaves and mist walls divide movement lanes.

11 — Phase 3

Corona brightness increases, parts of the arena darken, and reflected eclipse sigils become hazards.

12 — Boss Defeat

Fog retracts from the center.

13 — Veil Passage

The eclipse reflection becomes a silver portal path.

14 — Exit

Player crosses the basin and transitions to the next region.
