N. Collision / Navigation / Gameplay Readability

Keep the wet basin and main paths free of small collision snags.

Use simplified collision for fortress rubble and roots.

Deep water should be clearly differentiated from shallow traversal water.

The eclipse should remain visible at major route choices.

Do not allow dense dead-tree placement to create false pathways.

Use Nav Modifier Volumes around water hazards and temporary boss effects.

Reflective materials should never obscure attack telegraphs.

The fortress and tree silhouettes must remain readable from the basin after fog and VFX are added.

P. Performance Strategy

The highest risks are volumetric clouds, fog overdraw, reflective water, Lumen reflections, large Nanite hero assets, shadowed dead-tree fields, and boss-phase translucent VFX.

Use Nanite for fortress, cliffs, rocks, and the hero tree.

Use HISM/ISM for repeated background dead trees and rubble.

Keep the reflective basin material simple and avoid expensive multilayer translucency.

Use planar or high-quality reflections only where they provide visible value; let Lumen handle most reflections.

Reduce fog particle counts near camera.

Use distance culling for small tree silhouettes and debris.

Restrict shadow-casting local lights to beacons and a few critical props.

Use HLOD for mountain and fortress-background silhouettes.

Profile the final boss phase specifically, when water effects, fog, corona flare, particles, and boss attacks overlap.

Q. Development Roadmap
Stage 1 — Blockout

Build valley footprint, basin, fortress mass, tree mass, routes, ridges, player scale.

Stage 2 — Gameplay Validation

Test route choice, water movement, encounter spacing, sightlines, camera, boss arena.

Stage 3 — Structural Environment

Replace blockout with fortress modules, cliffs, hero tree, roots, dead-tree kit, basin geometry.

Stage 4 — Asset & Material Production

Finalize hero assets, rubble, shrine props, wet surfaces, fortress stone, water, decals.

Stage 5 — Lighting & Atmosphere

Build eclipse sky, silver rim lighting, clouds, mist, reflections, monochrome grade.

Stage 6 — Gameplay Implementation

Add beacons, barriers, hazards, boss logic, water shockwaves, final portal, streaming.

Stage 7 — Optimization & Polish

Profile Nanite, Lumen, water, fog, shadows, Niagara, collision, NavMesh, streaming, and cinematic polish.

Final Validation Checklist
  • Eclipse remains the dominant central landmark.
  • Black Spire Fortress stays on the left ridge.
  • Rootwatch Tree stays on the right ridge.
  • Basin remains the central traversal space.
  • Grayscale palette is preserved.
  • Silver-white eclipse light remains the main highlight.
  • Long sightlines remain readable.
  • Hero view matches the top-down map.
  • Fortress and tree routes reconnect logically.
  • Proposed dimensions remain consistent across panels.
  • Reflective water does not obscure gameplay.
  • Fog does not hide traversal boundaries.
  • Boss telegraphs remain readable on reflective surfaces.
  • NavMesh remains valid through boss phases.
  • Repeated trees use HISM/ISM where appropriate.
  • Nanite density is profiled.
  • Lumen reflection cost is controlled.
  • Volumetric fog/cloud settings have scalability tiers.
  • Background mountains remain non-playable.
  • Transition portal streams correctly.
  • Final UE5 build preserves the stark black-silver eclipse composition.
Open Design Questions
  • PC target frame rate.
  • Third-person or first-person camera.
  • Whether the two side objectives can be completed in either order.
  • Exact player movement speed in shallow water.
  • Whether swimming is supported.
  • Whether the Hollow Sentinel is humanoid, spectral, or environmental.
  • Desired level duration.
  • Whether the fortress contains interior rooms or remains mostly exterior.
  • Whether multiplayer/co-op needs support.
  • Whether the final eclipse portal is seamless streaming or a cinematic transition.

Aetherfall Basin — Valley Beneath the Verdant World

A primordial valley suspended beneath an enormous inhabited world, where floating landmasses and glowing waterways are held aloft by unknown celestial energy

Primary objective: Traverse the basin, activate three Aether Anchors, ascend to the suspended central sanctuary, survive the convergence event, and open the passage toward the upper world

OBSERVED: the scene is vertically layered, with a glowing river in the foreground, a broad floating landmass in the midground, waterfalls and cliffs on both sides, and a huge green planet filling the upper sky.

INFERRED: the floating central island naturally reads as the key mid-level objective or encounter space.

PROPOSED: the player begins near the river floor, ascends through canyon paths and suspended terrain, reaches the central floating sanctuary, then unlocks an upper-world transition.

B. Spatial & Gameplay Specification
Overall Layout

Z01 Emberwater Shore → Z02 Verdant Ravine → Z03 Lower Aether Falls → Z04 Floating Shelf Network → Z05 Central Sky Island → Z06 Celestial Convergence Shrine → Z07 Ascension Gate

The level should continually reinforce vertical progression. The player begins low in the valley and gradually climbs toward the floating island and sky.

Z01 — Emberwater Shore

Purpose: Establish scale and the celestial sky immediately.

Gameplay Function: Safe orientation and basic traversal.

Primary Visual Feature: Orange-gold water reflecting the horizon moon.

Encounter: None.

Traversal: Riverbank, shallow water, low rocks.

Player Experience: The upper green planet should appear impossibly large from this point.

Z02 — Verdant Ravine

Purpose: Introduce dense environmental navigation.

Gameplay Function: Exploration, first enemies, environmental storytelling.

Primary Feature: Tall cliff faces with hanging vegetation and waterfalls.

Encounter: Small roaming wildlife / corrupted creatures.

Traversal: Narrow paths, root bridges, rock ledges, shallow streams.

Optional Route: Behind a side waterfall into a cave.

Z03 — Lower Aether Falls

Purpose: Begin vertical ascent.

Gameplay Function: Platforming and environmental puzzle.

Primary Feature: Layered waterfalls cascading between cliff shelves.

Traversal: Stone terraces, climbable roots, broken natural bridges.

Encounter: Light ranged enemies positioned above the player.

Interactive Element: First Aether Anchor.

Z04 — Floating Shelf Network

Purpose: Introduce the environment’s signature traversal mechanic.

Gameplay Function: Suspended-island traversal, optional exploration, combat.

Primary Feature: Small and medium floating landmasses connected by broken stone bridges and energy lifts.

Encounter: Airborne enemies and one elite guardian.

Traversal: Jumps, bridges, moving fragments, ascension lifts.

Hazard: Falling into the valley below.

Z05 — Central Sky Island

Purpose: Major mid-level hub and second large visual reveal.

Gameplay Function: Combat, exploration, checkpoint, second and third Aether Anchors.

Primary Feature: Broad floating plateau with ancient vegetation and ruined celestial structures.

Encounter: Elite encounter or mini-boss.

Traversal: Open plateau with perimeter ledges and internal ruin corridors.

Z06 — Celestial Convergence Shrine

Purpose: Main climax.

Gameplay Function: Boss encounter / ritual activation.

Primary Feature: Shrine aligned visually with the green planet and horizon moon.

Encounter: Aetherbound Guardian.

Arena Behavior: The environment changes as celestial energy links the planet, moon, river, and floating islands.

Phase 1

Full arena usable.

Phase 2

Outer floating slabs detach and orbit the arena.

Phase 3

Golden river energy rises into the shrine while gravity becomes unstable in selected sectors.

Z07 — Ascension Gate

Purpose: Level exit.

Gameplay Function: Streaming transition to the next region.

Visual Feature: Vertical celestial beam linking the shrine to the giant overhead world.

Encounter: None.

Route Structure

Primary Route: River floor → ravine → waterfall ascent → floating shelf network → central sky island → shrine.

Secondary Route: Cliffside jungle trail bypassing part of the river.

Optional Route: Waterfall cavern leading to a high-value relic.

Secret Area: Underside cave beneath the central floating island, reachable through a controlled drop route or gravity lift.

Checkpoint 01: Lower Aether Falls.

Checkpoint 02: Floating Shelf Network.

Checkpoint 03: Central Sky Island.

Checkpoint 04: Post-boss shrine.

J. Environmental Storytelling

The valley should suggest it was once a connection point between the lower basin and the civilization visible or implied on the giant overhead world.

Story clues:

  • ruined towers positioned beneath floating islands;
  • ancient channels carrying glowing water toward the shrine;
  • broken Aether Anchors embedded in cliffs;
  • tree roots growing around abandoned technology;
  • floating stones clustered near former ritual sites;
  • waterfalls emerging from impossible suspended sources;
  • gold mineral lines converging toward the central island;
  • burned or crystallized vegetation close to unstable energy fields;
  • collapsed bridges indicating the route once served pilgrims or explorers;
  • small observatories aimed at the giant world above.

Audio: layered waterfalls, distant wind, rock creaks, sub-bass planetary resonance, floating debris collisions, insects in jungle zones, low Aether hum near anchors.

P. Performance Strategy

The primary risks are extreme vertical draw distance, large Nanite cliffs, multiple visible waterfalls, volumetric clouds, Lumen reflections, dense jungle foliage, floating-island silhouettes, and translucent VFX.

Use Nanite for large geology and ruin assets.

Use HISM/PCG for repeated vegetation, but hand-place all silhouette-critical trees.

Use HLOD for distant floating islands and canyon layers.

Use simplified distant waterfall materials rather than full Niagara systems.

Use Niagara culling and scalability tiers for mist, particles, and waterfall spray.

Keep hero water high quality only near the player; simplify distant river sections.

Use occlusion aggressively in ravine sections.

Avoid unnecessarily high shadow quality on distant vegetation.

Limit dynamic local lights around the shrine.

Profile the central floating island looking both upward toward the planet and downward through the canyon, because this view may expose the largest amount of geometry simultaneously.

Q. Development Roadmap
Stage 1 — Blockout

Valley footprint, cliffs, river, floating island, waterfall positions, routes, elevation.

Stage 2 — Gameplay Validation

Movement, jumping, vertical traversal, floating-platform timing, combat spacing, camera and sightlines.

Stage 3 — Structural Environment

Cliffs, island shells, riverbanks, bridges, shrine architecture, major vegetation masses.

Stage 4 — Asset & Material Production

Hero island, shrine, Aether Anchors, cliff kit, rocks, foliage, water and celestial materials.

Stage 5 — Lighting & Atmosphere

Planet illumination, moonlight, river glow, clouds, fog, waterfalls, atmospheric color grade.

Stage 6 — Gameplay Implementation

Anchors, gravity lifts, floating platforms, boss logic, arena changes, final ascension sequence.

Stage 7 — Optimization & Polish

Nanite, HLOD, Lumen, Niagara, water, foliage, collision, NavMesh, streaming, final cinematic pass.

Final Validation Checklist
  • Giant green planet remains the dominant upper landmark.
  • Warm secondary moon remains near the central horizon.
  • Valley retains strong vertical composition.
  • Central floating island remains visible from major lower viewpoints.
  • River provides a clear foreground navigation line.
  • Waterfalls retain correct cliff relationships.
  • Floating islands remain spatially consistent across every panel.
  • Top-down map and side section describe the same level.
  • Vertical traversal is feasible at player scale.
  • Background floating islands remain non-playable unless explicitly mapped.
  • Teal/green and amber lighting hierarchy is preserved.
  • Major traversal edges remain readable.
  • Waterfall mist does not hide landings.
  • Moving islands use safe predictable collision.
  • NavMesh remains valid in combat areas.
  • Nanite density is profiled.
  • Distant islands use HLOD.
  • Niagara uses distance/scalability controls.
  • Foliage uses HISM/PCG appropriately.
  • Lumen cost is measured in vertical vistas.
  • Final boss phase remains within VFX budget.
  • Ascension transition streams correctly.
  • Hero environment, maps, assets, dimensions, lighting and gameplay remain internally consistent.
Open Design Questions
  • PC target frame rate.
  • Third-person or first-person camera.
  • Player jump, mantle and climbing capabilities.
  • Whether falling from floating islands means instant death or recovery.
  • Whether the player has a grapple / air-dash / glide mechanic.
  • Combat density compared with exploration.
  • Exact boss archetype.
  • Intended level duration.
  • Multiplayer/co-op requirements.
  • Whether the final ascension leads seamlessly to the planet above or uses a cinematic transition.

OBSERVED: the main composition uses the bridge as a visual and navigational line leading directly toward the castle, while giant trees frame both sides and the moon sits almost directly above the destination.

INFERRED: the winding bridge naturally becomes the primary traversal route, with the ravine and tree-side structures supporting optional exploration.

PROPOSED: three lantern shrines placed along the route progressively reactivate the settlement and unlock the citadel entrance.

B. Spatial & Gameplay Specification

Overall Level Flow

Z01 Lanternwood Entry → Z02 Moonbridge Approach → Z03 Ravine Hamlet → Z04 Whispering Tree District → Z05 Citadel Steps → Z06 Moonveil Court → Z07 Lunar Gate

The level should feel forward-readable but vertically layered. The player can always understand the castle as the destination, while side paths create discovery without breaking orientation.

Z01 — Lanternwood Entry

Purpose: Establish the moon, bridge, giant trees, and distant citadel.

Gameplay Function: Safe introduction and movement tutorial.

Primary Visual Feature: First full reveal of the winding bridge.

Encounter: None.

Traversal: Broad wooden path and stone verge.

Storytelling: Abandoned lantern posts imply the path was once ceremonial.

Z02 — Moonbridge Approach

Purpose: Introduce the signature traversal route.

Gameplay Function: First light combat and first Lantern Shrine.

Primary Visual Feature: Elevated bridge crossing above the dark ravine.

Encounter: Small shadow-creature or corrupted sentinel group.

Traversal: Bridge walk, broken planks, narrow side platforms.

Hazard: Falling into ravine.

Z03 — Ravine Hamlet

Purpose: Add social/architectural density.

Gameplay Function: Exploration, optional lore, checkpoint, second Lantern Shrine.

Primary Visual Feature: Small warm-lit cliff houses beneath giant trees.

Encounter: Optional ambush or NPC interaction depending on story direction.

Traversal: Stairs, side paths, short suspended walkways.

Optional Route: Interior house or workshop with reward.

Z04 — Whispering Tree District

Purpose: Shift from settlement to mystical upper route.

Gameplay Function: Vertical traversal and environmental puzzle.

Primary Visual Feature: Huge twisted tree with lanterns suspended from branches.

Encounter: Elite spirit guardian.

Traversal: Root ramps, branch bridges, narrow platforms.

Interaction: Third Lantern Shrine.

Z05 — Citadel Steps

Purpose: Final approach.

Gameplay Function: Combat escalation.

Primary Visual Feature: Citadel facade growing larger while bridge narrows into ceremonial steps.

Encounter: Mixed enemy group or elite sentinels.

Traversal: Stone stairs, bridge arches, gate platforms.

Z06 — Moonveil Court

Purpose: Climax arena.

Gameplay Function: Boss / ritual encounter.

Primary Visual Feature: Central moon-aligned courtyard before the citadel.

Encounter: Warden of Moonveil.

Arena Style: Broad circular/oval stone plaza, shallow reflective water channels, lantern pylons.

Z07 — Lunar Gate

Purpose: Level transition.

Gameplay Function: Reward and streaming handoff.

Visual Feature: Moonlight-focused portal inside or behind the citadel.

Route Structure

Primary Route: Entry → Moonbridge → Hamlet → Tree District → Citadel → Court.

Secondary Route: Hamlet lower path → ravine overlook → reconnect near Tree District.

Optional Route: Branch path through a lantern house or shrine pavilion.

Secret Area: A hidden moon shrine beneath the bridge, accessed from a lower ledge.

Checkpoints:

CP01 — Moonbridge midpoint

CP02 — Ravine Hamlet

CP03 — Citadel Steps

CP04 — Post-boss Lunar Gate

Playable Boundaries

Use:

  • steep ravine walls,
  • untraversable giant roots,
  • locked house interiors,
  • cliff edges,
  • dense canopy,
  • deep fog below the bridge,
  • citadel walls.

Avoid obvious invisible walls where natural geometry can communicate the boundary.

The image depends on a strong cool moonlight vs warm lantern contrast.

J. Environmental Storytelling

The settlement should imply that the Moonveil route was once a ceremonial pilgrimage road leading to the citadel.

Story clues:

  • bridge lanterns decrease in brightness away from active shrines;
  • houses contain abandoned offerings;
  • tree roots grow around older bridge supports;
  • moon symbols repeat on railings, shrine stones, roof crests and citadel doors;
  • some lanterns are broken or dark;
  • collapsed side paths imply parts of the settlement have been abandoned;
  • ceremonial banners survive only near the citadel;
  • the ravine contains remnants of older bridges;
  • one tree contains carved names of previous pilgrims.

Audio opportunities: bridge wood creaks, wind in canopy, chain/lantern chimes, distant water, soft insects, moonlit hum near shrines, low citadel bells.

N. Collision / Navigation / Gameplay Readability

Bridge collision should be simple, continuous, and independent from decorative railings.

Avoid snagging on lantern posts and root decorations.

Use invisible blocking geometry to keep players from stepping through rail gaps that appear safe.

Ravine fall zones require consistent telegraphing.

Enemy NavMesh should cover bridge plazas, hamlet zones and Moonveil Court, but not decorative roofs or narrow branch geometry.

Warm lanterns should naturally identify safe traversal surfaces.

The citadel must remain visible at key decision points.

P. Performance Strategy

The biggest risks are large night-time draw distances, dense tree canopies, dozens of local lantern lights, volumetric fog, Lumen bounce, shadowed architecture, and translucent particle effects.

Use Nanite for cliffs, citadel stone, bridge supports and hero tree trunks.

Use HISM for repeated lantern posts, small trees, roof props and decorative assets.

Do not make every lantern a shadow-casting light; reserve true lights for important path markers and shrines, with emissive-only materials for secondary lamps.

Use VFX culling for fireflies, leaves and mist.

Use HLOD for distant village buildings and citadel substructures.

Restrict volumetric fog density below bridge level.

Use material instances instead of unique shaders for each house.

Profile the main bridge looking directly toward the illuminated citadel, because that view includes the moon, city lights, foliage, fog, bridge geometry and most distant architecture simultaneously.

Q. Development Roadmap
Stage 1 — Blockout

Bridge route, ravine depth, village zones, hero trees, citadel silhouette, courtyard.

Stage 2 — Gameplay Validation

Movement, bridge width, combat spacing, vertical traversal, camera, fall hazards, sightlines.

Stage 3 — Structural Environment

Bridge kit, cliffs, house modules, tree roots, citadel architecture.

Stage 4 — Asset & Material Production

Lanterns, shrine props, hero tree, village assets, materials, decals and wetness.

Stage 5 — Lighting & Atmosphere

Moon lighting, lantern network, volumetric mist, sky, clouds, warm/cool color grade.

Stage 6 — Gameplay Implementation

Shrines, gates, optional paths, arena controller, boss phases, final Lunar Gate.

Stage 7 — Optimization & Polish

Nanite, Lumen, HISM, fog, VFX, lighting cost, collision, NavMesh, HLOD, streaming and final cinematic polish.

Final Validation Checklist
  • Giant moon remains the dominant sky landmark.
  • Citadel stays centered at the end of the bridge route.
  • Main bridge remains the strongest navigational line.
  • Giant trees continue to frame the composition.
  • Warm lanterns contrast clearly with cool moonlight.
  • Ravine depth remains visually readable.
  • Optional paths do not obscure the primary route.
  • Top-down map matches the same bridge/citadel geometry.
  • Citadel size remains consistent across hero and gameplay views.
  • Lantern Shrine positions match progression.
  • Bridge dimensions remain consistent.
  • Player scale reads correctly.
  • Foliage does not block traversal.
  • Railings and decorative roots do not create snagging.
  • Warm lights do not overwhelm moonlight.
  • Boss effects preserve attack readability.
  • Lumen cost is profiled.
  • Shadow-casting lantern count is controlled.
  • Niagara uses culling/scalability.
  • HLOD handles distant village/citadel structures.
  • Ravine mist stays below critical traversal visibility.
  • Final Lunar Gate streams correctly.
  • Poster and written specification remain internally consistent.
Open Design Questions
  • PC target frame rate.
  • Third-person or first-person camera.
  • Whether the settlement has friendly NPCs or is abandoned.
  • Whether bridge traversal includes jumping/mantling.
  • Whether falling into the ravine is instant death or recoverable.
  • Exact combat density.
  • Whether the Warden is humanoid, spirit, or construct.
  • Desired total level duration.
  • Multiplayer/co-op support.
  • Whether the Lunar Gate loads seamlessly or through a cinematic transition.

ENVIRONMENT 09 · UE5 PRODUCTION PLAN

Crimson Eclipse Capital — Palace of the Ashen Sun

A vast imperial city built beneath a corrupted celestial eclipse, where the entire capital is aligned toward a monumental palace that channels the dying sun

Primary objective: Cross the lower lantern district, reactivate three Eclipse Seals, ascend through the capital, defeat the Palace Warden, and enter the inner sanctum beneath the black sun

Read full production specification · 19 sections
A. Level Overview
ItemProduction Definition
Level NameCrimson Eclipse Capital — Palace of the Ashen Sun
Level CategoryDense fantasy capital / ceremonial ascent / urban combat / palace boss approach
ThemeA vast imperial city built beneath a corrupted celestial eclipse, where the entire capital is aligned toward a monumental palace that channels the dying sun
Gameplay TypeCity traversal → district exploration → street combat → rooftop/terrace ascent → palace approach → boss encounter → eclipse gate transition
Primary ObjectiveCross the lower lantern district, reactivate three Eclipse Seals, ascend through the capital, defeat the Palace Warden, and enter the inner sanctum beneath the black sun
Main LandmarkMassive tiered imperial palace/citadel aligned beneath the black celestial orb
Secondary LandmarksLong lantern avenue, stacked pagoda roofs, ceremonial gates, stepped terraces, rooftop ridges, bridge approaches, eclipse-aligned towers
Intended ExperienceGrandeur → intimidation → urban discovery → rising pressure → ceremonial ascent → supernatural climax
Visual IdentityDeep navy/charcoal architecture, warm orange-red lanterns, smoky blue atmosphere, black eclipse disk with incandescent orange-red corona
Reference Elements to PreserveCentral axial avenue, layered roof silhouettes, palace position, eclipsed sun, lone player scale, dense city terraces, warm/cool contrast, monumental depth

OBSERVED: the composition is strongly axial. The player stands on a broad stone avenue that leads directly through successive architectural layers toward the palace, while the black-red celestial body crowns the skyline.

INFERRED: the avenue naturally functions as the primary navigation spine, while side streets and terraces support optional exploration.

PROPOSED: the level becomes a rising urban gauntlet in which three Eclipse Seals unlock the palace and progressively intensify the celestial phenomenon.

B. Spatial & Gameplay Specification
Overall Layout

Z01 Ashen Gate → Z02 Lantern Market → Z03 Processional Avenue → Z04 Lower Terrace District → Z05 Eclipse Temple Ward → Z06 Palace Causeway → Z07 Palace Forecourt → Z08 Inner Eclipse Gate

The entire level should preserve a visible relationship between the player and the palace. Even when the route bends through side districts, the palace and eclipse should repeatedly reappear as orientation landmarks.

Z01 — Ashen Gate

Purpose: Establish scale and introduce the city.

Gameplay Function: Safe orientation, first NPC/lore interactions.

Primary Visual Feature: Full view down the ceremonial avenue.

Encounter: None.

Traversal: Broad stone paving, stairs, side alleys.

Z02 — Lantern Market

Purpose: Add urban density and lived-in storytelling.

Gameplay Function: Exploration, optional vendors/lore, first combat.

Primary Visual Feature: Dense rows of warm lanterns beneath overhanging tiled roofs.

Encounter: Small patrol or shadow-creature ambush.

Traversal: Main street plus two side alleys.

Z03 — Processional Avenue

Purpose: Main cinematic approach.

Gameplay Function: Medium combat lane, checkpoint, first Eclipse Seal.

Primary Visual Feature: Long symmetrical street framed by rooftops and gate towers.

Encounter: Mixed melee/ranged wave.

Traversal: Wide central lane with lateral side streets.

Z04 — Lower Terrace District

Purpose: Break the linearity with layered vertical movement.

Gameplay Function: Exploration, rooftop traversal, second Seal.

Primary Visual Feature: Stacked terraces and stepped rooftops.

Encounter: Elite patrol.

Traversal: Stairs, balconies, rooftop bridges, narrow alleys.

Z05 — Eclipse Temple Ward

Purpose: Supernatural escalation.

Gameplay Function: Environmental puzzle / combat ritual.

Primary Visual Feature: Shrine complex directly aligned to the eclipse.

Encounter: Ritual guardians.

Interaction: Third Eclipse Seal.

Z06 — Palace Causeway

Purpose: Re-establish the monumental centerline.

Gameplay Function: High-pressure combat and final approach.

Primary Visual Feature: Palace filling most of the forward view.

Encounter: Heavy elite enemies.

Traversal: Broad stairs, bridges, gatehouses.

Z07 — Palace Forecourt

Purpose: Main boss arena.

Gameplay Function: Palace Warden encounter.

Primary Visual Feature: Massive palace facade, ceremonial court, eclipse halo directly above.

Arena Style: Large rectangular court with side terraces and central ceremonial path.

Z08 — Inner Eclipse Gate

Purpose: Level transition.

Gameplay Function: Reward, final interaction, streaming handoff.

Visual Feature: Circular eclipse-aligned energy gateway behind the palace doors.

Route Structure

Primary Route: Gate → Market → Avenue → Temple Ward → Causeway → Forecourt.

Secondary Route: Lower Terrace District rooftop path.

Optional Route: Side shrine lane through artisan houses and a hidden courtyard.

Secret Area: Locked memorial chamber beneath a terrace stair, accessible after activating the second Seal.

Checkpoints:

CP01 — Lantern Market exit

CP02 — Processional Avenue midpoint

CP03 — Eclipse Temple Ward

CP04 — Palace Forecourt entrance

CP05 — Post-boss Inner Gate

Playable Boundaries

Use dense architecture, walls, locked doors, rooftop drop-offs, deep alleys, canal/void gaps, and palace walls rather than obvious invisible barriers.

Background Scenery

Upper palace towers, distant roof fields, far mountain silhouettes, and high skyline architecture remain background-only unless explicitly mapped.

J. Environmental Storytelling

The city should imply that it was once a prosperous imperial capital whose religion and political power were built around celestial cycles.

Story clues include inactive shrines along the avenue, cracked eclipse motifs on paving stones, old festival lanterns left hanging, abandoned market stalls, sealed palace side gates, soot accumulation on upper roofs, ceremonial banners near the palace, weapon damage near guard posts, and increased supernatural distortion closer to the Eclipse Temple.

Audio opportunities: distant bells, wooden roof creaks, cloth banners in wind, soft street chatter or echoes, ash hiss, lantern crackle, low eclipse resonance, metallic gate movement, palace drums during escalation.

N. Collision / Navigation / Gameplay Readability

Keep the main avenue collision simple and continuous.

Use dedicated traversal collision for stairs and rooftop routes rather than relying on detailed Nanite geometry.

Avoid small decorative roof edges creating snag points.

Use invisible blockers where roof shapes visually imply impassable surfaces.

Enemy NavMesh should cover streets, terraces and forecourt, but not decorative roofs unless deliberately playable.

Warm lantern lighting should identify primary safe routes; red/orange eclipse effects should be reserved for danger and progression states.

P. Performance Strategy

The biggest likely costs are dense urban draw distance, repeated roofs, large Nanite palace geometry, hundreds of lanterns, dynamic shadows, Lumen, volumetric atmosphere, and eclipse VFX.

Use Nanite for hero architecture and large stone/timber assemblies.

Use HISM for lanterns, repeated roof ornaments, columns, and props.

Only a limited subset of lanterns should cast dynamic shadows; most should use emissive materials with low-cost local lighting.

Use HLOD for distant roof clusters.

Use occlusion aggressively through district turns and gatehouses.

Keep volumetric fog concentrated in lower streets rather than covering the entire city.

Use VFX distance culling and scalability.

Profile the main avenue looking uphill toward the palace and eclipse, because that camera exposes the most architecture, lights, fog, VFX, and distant geometry simultaneously.

Q. Development Roadmap
Stage 1 — Blockout

Avenue, district footprints, terrace elevations, palace massing, gate positions, player scale.

Stage 2 — Gameplay Validation

Route clarity, rooftop movement, combat spacing, camera, boss arena, checkpoints.

Stage 3 — Structural Environment

Street kit, house modules, roof kit, gates, palace terraces, temple structures.

Stage 4 — Asset & Material Production

Lanterns, seals, props, banners, stone/timber/roof materials, wear decals.

Stage 5 — Lighting & Atmosphere

Night sky, eclipse, lantern network, fog, color grade, ash VFX.

Stage 6 — Gameplay Implementation

Seals, gates, shortcuts, enemy spawning, boss logic, final Eclipse Gate.

Stage 7 — Optimization & Polish

Nanite, Lumen, HISM, lighting cost, HLOD, Niagara, collision, NavMesh, streaming, final cinematic polish.

Final Validation Checklist
  • Eclipse remains aligned with the palace.
  • Palace stays the primary architectural focal point.
  • Main avenue remains the strongest traversal line.
  • Dense roof layers match the reference silhouette.
  • Warm lanterns contrast clearly with cool night ambience.
  • Red eclipse effects remain visually distinct from ordinary lantern lighting.
  • Top-down map matches the same district layout.
  • Rooftop routes remain secondary to the main avenue.
  • Palace scale stays consistent across views.
  • Seal locations match gameplay progression.
  • Player scale reads correctly against palace and avenue.
  • Collision does not snag on stairs or roof details.
  • NavMesh supports all combat spaces.
  • Lantern count and dynamic shadow cost are controlled.
  • HLOD handles distant roof fields.
  • Niagara uses scalability and culling.
  • Volumetric fog does not obscure route readability.
  • Boss VFX preserve attack telegraphs.
  • Final gate transition streams correctly.
  • Poster and written specification describe the same level.
Open Design Questions
  • PC target frame rate.
  • Third-person or first-person camera.
  • Whether the capital is populated or abandoned.
  • Whether players can enter house interiors.
  • Exact rooftop traversal abilities.
  • Combat density through the lower city.
  • Palace Warden archetype.
  • Intended level duration.
  • Multiplayer/co-op requirements.
  • Whether the Eclipse Gate uses seamless streaming or a cinematic transition.
